sentences.zh: 隱逸上

translations.literal: Recluses, Part One
translations.idiomatic: Recluses, Part One

sentences.zh: ○戚同文陳摶種放萬適李瀆魏野邢敦林逋高懌徐復孔文何群

translations.literal: ○ Qi Tongwen, Chen Tuan, Zhong Fang, Wan Shi, Li Du, Wei Ye, Xing Dun, Lin Bu, Gao Yi, Xu Fu, Kong Wen, He Qun
translations.idiomatic: ○ Qi Tongwen, Chen Tuan, Zhong Fang, Wan Shi, Li Du, Wei Ye, Xing Dun, Lin Bu, Gao Yi, Xu Fu, Kong Wen, and He Qun

sentences.zh: 中古聖人之作《易》也，於《遁》之上九曰「肥遁，無不利」，《蠱》之上九曰「不事王侯，高尚其事」。

translations.literal: When the sage of middle antiquity composed the Changes, in the top line of Dun he wrote, "A fat retreat—nothing is unfavorable," and in the top line of Gu he wrote, "He does not serve kings and lords; he elevates his own affairs."
translations.idiomatic: When the ancient sage composed the Book of Changes, the top line of the hexagram Dun reads, "A full withdrawal—nothing is unfavorable," and the top line of Gu reads, "He does not serve kings and lords; he exalts his own calling."

sentences.zh: 二爻以陽德處高地，而皆以隱逸當之。

translations.literal: Both lines, with yang virtue in a high position, are taken to represent reclusion.
translations.idiomatic: Both lines embody yang virtue in the highest place, and both are understood as figures of withdrawal from the world.

sentences.zh: 然則隱德之高於當世，其來也遠矣。

translations.literal: Thus the loftiness of the virtue of reclusion above the age has come from far back.
translations.idiomatic: The elevation of reclusive virtue above ordinary society, then, has roots reaching far into the past.

sentences.zh: 巢、由雖不見於經，其可誣哉。

translations.literal: Chao and You, though they do not appear in the classics, how could one deny them?
translations.idiomatic: Chao Fu and Xu You do not appear in the canonical texts, yet who could dismiss their example as mere legend?

sentences.zh: 五季之亂，避世宜多。

translations.literal: In the chaos of the Five Dynasties, it was fitting that many should withdraw from the world.
translations.idiomatic: During the turmoil of the Five Dynasties, it was only natural that many would turn away from public life.

sentences.zh: 宋興，岩穴弓旌之招，疊見於史，然而高蹈遠引若陳摶者，終莫得而致之，豈非二卦之上九者乎？

translations.literal: When the Song arose, invitations with bow and banner to men in caves and cliffs repeatedly appear in the histories; yet one who strode high and drew far away, like Chen Tuan, in the end could not be brought in—were they not indeed the top lines of those two hexagrams?
translations.idiomatic: After the Song rose to power, records repeatedly mention summons by bow and banner to recluses in mountain caves—yet men of the highest withdrawal, such as Chen Tuan, could never finally be brought to court. Were they not living embodiments of those two upper lines?

sentences.zh: 种放之徒，召對大廷，亹獻替，使其人出處，果有合於《艮》之君子時止時行，人何譏焉。

translations.literal: Men like Zhong Fang were summoned to audience in the great court and diligently offered remonstrance and replacement; if such men's coming forth and withdrawal truly accorded with the noble person of Gen—stopping at the right time and acting at the right time—who could reproach them?
translations.idiomatic: Men such as Zhong Fang were called to the imperial audience hall and earnestly offered counsel and correction; when their decisions to serve or withdraw truly matched the noble person of the Gen hexagram—knowing when to stop and when to act—who could fault them?

sentences.zh: 作《隱逸傳》。

translations.literal: Therefore the "Biographies of Recluses" was composed.
translations.idiomatic: On this basis the "Biographies of Recluses" was written.

sentences.zh: 戚同文

translations.literal: Qi Tongwen
translations.idiomatic: Qi Tongwen

sentences.zh: 戚同文，字同文，宋之楚丘人。

translations.literal: Qi Tongwen, styled Tongwen, was a man of Chuqiu in Song.
translations.idiomatic: Qi Tongwen, whose style was Tongwen, came from Chuqiu in the state of Song.

sentences.zh: 世為儒。

translations.literal: His family for generations were Confucian scholars.
translations.idiomatic: His family had been scholars for generations.

sentences.zh: 幼孤，祖母攜育於外氏，奉養以孝聞。

translations.literal: Orphaned young, his grandmother took and raised him at her maiden family's home; his filial support became known.
translations.idiomatic: He lost his parents in childhood, and his grandmother raised him at her own family's home; he became renowned for the filial care he gave her.

sentences.zh: 祖母卒，晝夜哀號，不食數日，鄉里為之感動。

translations.literal: When his grandmother died, he wailed day and night and did not eat for several days; the village was moved by it.
translations.idiomatic: When his grandmother died, he mourned day and night and refused food for several days, moving everyone in the neighborhood.

sentences.zh: 始，聞邑人楊愨教授生徒，日過其學舍，因授《禮記》，隨即成誦，日諷一卷，愨異而留之。

translations.literal: At first, hearing that a townsman, Yang Min, was instructing pupils, he daily passed by the schoolhouse; because he was taught the Record of Rites, he could recite it at once, reciting one scroll per day—Min marveled and kept him.
translations.idiomatic: At first he heard that a fellow townsman, Yang Min, was teaching students. He passed the schoolhouse every day, received instruction in the Record of Rites, and could recite each passage as soon as he heard it, mastering one scroll a day. Min was astonished and took him in as a student.

sentences.zh: 不終歲畢誦《五經》，愨即妻以女弟。

translations.literal: Before the year was out he had finished reciting the Five Classics; Min then gave him his younger sister in marriage.
translations.idiomatic: Before a year had passed he had memorized the Five Classics, and Min gave him his younger sister in marriage.

sentences.zh: 自是彌益勤勵讀書，累年不解帶。

translations.literal: From then on he read with ever greater diligence, for many years not loosening his belt.
translations.idiomatic: From then on he threw himself ever more zealously into study, going for years without even loosening his belt at night.

sentences.zh: 時晉末喪亂，絕意祿仕，且思見混一，遂以「同文」為名字。

translations.literal: At the time, in the disorders at the end of Jin, he set his mind against salary and office, and moreover longed to see unification—therefore he took "Tongwen" as his style and name.
translations.idiomatic: In the chaos at the end of the Jin period he renounced all thought of official salary, and because he yearned to see the realm united under one rule, he adopted Tongwen as both his style and his name.

sentences.zh: 愨嘗勉之仕，同文曰：「長者不仕，同文亦不仕。」

translations.literal: Min once urged him to take office; Tongwen said, "If my elder does not serve, Tongwen also will not serve."
translations.idiomatic: Min once urged him to enter government service. Tongwen replied, "If my elder does not serve, I shall not serve either."

sentences.zh: 愨依將軍趙直家，遇疾不起，以家事托同文，即為葬三世數喪。

translations.literal: Min lodged with the general Zhao Zhi's household, fell ill and could not rise, entrusted family affairs to Tongwen, and Tongwen at once buried several funerals spanning three generations.
translations.idiomatic: Min had been living in the household of General Zhao Zhi when he fell gravely ill. He entrusted his family affairs to Tongwen, who immediately undertook the burial of several members of three generations of the family.

sentences.zh: 直復厚加禮待，為築室聚徒，請益之人不遠千里而至。

translations.literal: Zhi again treated him with great courtesy, built a hall and gathered pupils; those who came to seek instruction did not regard a thousand li as far.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi treated him with still greater respect, built a hall for him, and gathered students around him. Learners came from a thousand li away to seek his teaching.

sentences.zh: 登第者五六十人，宗度、許驤、陳象輿、高象先、郭成範、王礪、滕涉皆踐台閣。

translations.literal: Those who passed the examinations numbered fifty or sixty; Zong Du, Xu Xiang, Chen Xiangyu, Gao Xiangxian, Guo Chengfan, Wang Li, and Teng She all reached the halls of state.
translations.idiomatic: Fifty or sixty of his students passed the civil examinations, and among them Zong Du, Xu Xiang, Chen Xiangyu, Gao Xiangxian, Guo Chengfan, Wang Li, and Teng She all rose to high positions at court.

sentences.zh: 同文純質尚信義，人有喪者力拯濟之，宗族閭里貧乏者周給之。

translations.literal: Tongwen was pure in character and valued faith and righteousness; when anyone had a funeral he strove to aid them, and to kinsmen and neighbors in poverty he gave comprehensive relief.
translations.idiomatic: Tongwen was plain and sincere, and held faith and righteousness above all else. He did his utmost to help anyone who faced a funeral, and he provided generously for poor kinsmen and neighbors.

sentences.zh: 冬月，多解衣裘與寒者。

translations.literal: In winter months he often took off his fur coat and gave it to those who were cold.
translations.idiomatic: In winter he would often take off his own fur coat and give it to someone who was shivering with cold.

sentences.zh: 不積財，不營居室，或勉之，輒曰：「人生以行義為貴，焉用此為！」

translations.literal: He did not amass wealth or build a dwelling; when some urged him, he would say, "In human life, acting righteously is what is precious—what use is this!"
translations.idiomatic: He neither hoarded wealth nor built himself a fine house. When people urged him to do so, he would say, "What matters in life is righteous conduct—what need is there for such things!"

sentences.zh: 由是深為鄉里推服。

translations.literal: Because of this he was deeply esteemed in the village.
translations.idiomatic: For this reason the whole neighborhood held him in the deepest respect.

sentences.zh: 有不循孝悌者，同文必諭以善道。

translations.literal: When anyone did not follow filial piety and brotherly duty, Tongwen always instructed them in the good way.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he found someone neglecting filial piety or brotherly duty, Tongwen would counsel them on the right path.

sentences.zh: 頗有知人鑒，所與遊皆一時名士。

translations.literal: He had considerable discernment in knowing men; all with whom he associated were eminent men of the time.
translations.idiomatic: He had a keen eye for character, and everyone he befriended was a leading figure of the day.

sentences.zh: 樂聞人善，未嘗言人短。

translations.literal: He delighted to hear of others' goodness and never spoke of others' faults.
translations.idiomatic: He took pleasure in hearing of others' virtues and never spoke of their failings.

sentences.zh: 與宗翼、張昉、滕知白為友。

translations.literal: He was friends with Zong Yi, Zhang Fang, and Teng Zhibai.
translations.idiomatic: His close friends included Zong Yi, Zhang Fang, and Teng Zhibai.

sentences.zh: 生平不至京師。

translations.literal: In his whole life he never went to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Throughout his life he never once traveled to the capital.

sentences.zh: 長子維任隨州書記，迎同文就養，卒於漢東，年七十三。

translations.literal: His eldest son Wei served as secretary of Suizhou, welcomed Tongwen to be supported by him, and Tongwen died in Handong at age seventy-three.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Wei held the post of secretary in Suizhou and brought Tongwen home to live under his care. Tongwen died in Handong at the age of seventy-three.

sentences.zh: 好為詩，有《孟諸集》二十卷。

translations.literal: He loved to compose poetry and had a collection in twenty scrolls entitled Mengzhu ji.
translations.idiomatic: He loved to write poetry and left a twenty-scroll collection entitled Collected Works from Mengzhu.

sentences.zh: 楊徽之嘗因使至郡，一見相善，多與酬唱。

translations.literal: Yang Huizhi once came to the commandery on a mission; at one meeting they took a liking to each other and often exchanged poems in reply.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Huizhi once came to the prefecture on official business. The two men took an immediate liking to each other and exchanged many poems in correspondence.

sentences.zh: 徽之嘗雲陶隱居號堅白先生，先生純粹質直，以道義自富，遂與其門人追號堅素先生。

translations.literal: Huizhi once said that Tao Hongjing styled himself Master Firm-and-White; this master was pure and plain in character, enriching himself through the Way and righteousness—therefore he and his disciples posthumously styled him Master Firm-and-Simple.
translations.idiomatic: Huizhi remarked that Tao Hongjing had taken the sobriquet Master Firm-and-White. Tongwen was pure and upright in character and found his wealth in the Way and in righteousness, so Huizhi and his disciples posthumously honored him as Master Firm-and-Simple.

sentences.zh: 二子維、綸。

translations.literal: He had two sons, Wei and Lun.
translations.idiomatic: He had two sons, Wei and Lun.

sentences.zh: 維，建隆二年，以屯田員外郎為曹王府翊善，累官職方郎中，致仕，卒，年八十一。

translations.literal: Wei, in the second year of Jianlong, was made companion to the Prince of Cao as an outer gentleman of the Directorate of Agriculture, rose through offices to Director of Works bureau director, retired, and died at age eighty-one.
translations.idiomatic: Wei, in the second year of the Jianlong reign (961), was appointed companion to the Prince of Cao with the rank of outer gentleman in the Directorate of Agriculture. He rose to director in the Bureau of Works, retired from office, and died at the age of eighty-one.

sentences.zh: 綸自有傳。

translations.literal: Lun has his own biography.
translations.idiomatic: Lun has a separate biography of his own.

sentences.zh: 大中祥符二年，府民曹城即同文舊居旁造舍百餘區，聚書數千卷，延生徒講習甚盛。

translations.literal: In the second year of Dazhong Xiangfu, a man of the prefecture, Cao Cheng, beside Tongwen's old residence built more than a hundred rooms, gathered several thousand scrolls of books, and extended instruction to pupils with great flourishing.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of the Dazhong Xiangfu era (1009), a local man named Cao Cheng built more than a hundred rooms beside Tongwen's former home, assembled several thousand scrolls of books, and ran a thriving school for students.

sentences.zh: 詔賜額為本府書院，命綸子奉禮郎舜賓主之，署誠府助教，委本府幕官提舉之。

translations.literal: An edict granted it a plaque as the prefectural academy; Lun's son, the director of ceremonies Shunbin, was ordered to preside over it, appointed assistant instructor of the prefecture of Gui, and a staff officer of the prefecture was entrusted to supervise it.
translations.idiomatic: An imperial edict granted the school an official name as the prefectural academy. Tongwen's grandson Shunbin, holder of the rank of director of ceremonies, was placed in charge, given the title of assistant instructor of Gui Prefecture, and oversight was assigned to a staff officer of the prefecture.

sentences.zh: 楊愨者，虞城人。

translations.literal: Yang Min was a man of Yucheng.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Min came from Yucheng.

sentences.zh: 力學勤志，不求聞達。

translations.literal: He studied with vigor and was diligent in purpose, not seeking fame or advancement.
translations.idiomatic: He studied with tireless dedication and sought neither fame nor advancement.

sentences.zh: 宗翼者，蔡州上蔡人。

translations.literal: Zong Yi was a man of Shangcai in Cai Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Zong Yi came from Shangcai in Cai Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 父為虞城主簿，因家焉。

translations.literal: His father was registrar of Yucheng, and so the family settled there.
translations.idiomatic: His father served as registrar of Yucheng, and the family made their home there.

sentences.zh: 篤孝恭謹，負米養母。

translations.literal: Deep in filial piety, respectful and cautious, he carried rice on his back to support his mother.
translations.idiomatic: Deeply filial, respectful, and careful, he carried rice on his back to support his mother.

sentences.zh: 好學強記，經籍一見即能默寫。

translations.literal: He loved learning and had a powerful memory; after one look at a classic text he could write it out from memory.
translations.idiomatic: He loved learning and had an extraordinary memory. After a single reading of a classic text he could reproduce it from memory.

sentences.zh: 歐陽、虞、柳書皆得其楷法。

translations.literal: In the calligraphy of Ouyang, Yu, and Liu he mastered all their regular-script methods.
translations.idiomatic: He mastered the regular-script styles of Ouyang Xun, Yu Shinan, and Liu Gongquan.

sentences.zh: 能屬文。

translations.literal: He could compose literary pieces.
translations.idiomatic: He was also skilled at literary composition.

sentences.zh: 隱而不仕，家無鬥粟，怡怡如也，未嘗以貧窶幹人。

translations.literal: He lived in reclusion and did not take office; his household had not a peck of grain, yet he was cheerful and at ease, never troubling others because of poverty.
translations.idiomatic: He lived in seclusion and never took office. His household scarcely had a peck of grain, yet he remained cheerful and serene and never importuned others because of his poverty.

sentences.zh: 市物不評價，市人知而不欺。

translations.literal: When he bought goods he did not haggle over price; the market people knew him and did not cheat him.
translations.idiomatic: When he bought goods in the market he never haggled over price, and the merchants, knowing his character, never cheated him.

sentences.zh: 嘗言「晝夜者，昏曉之辨也」，故既暝未曙，皆不出戶。

translations.literal: He once said, "Day and night are the distinction between dusk and dawn," and therefore between twilight and daybreak he never went out of doors.
translations.idiomatic: He once remarked, "Day and night mark the boundary between dusk and dawn," and for that reason he never left his house between nightfall and first light.

sentences.zh: 見鄰裏小兒，待之如成人，未嘗欺紿。

translations.literal: When he met neighborhood children he treated them as adults and never deceived or teased them.
translations.idiomatic: When he met the neighborhood children he treated them as seriously as adults and never teased or deceived them.

sentences.zh: 同文嘗謂翼曰：「子勞謙有古人風，真吾友也。」

translations.literal: Tongwen once said to Yi, "You are diligent and modest and have the air of the ancients—you are truly my friend."
translations.idiomatic: Tongwen once told Yi, "You are diligent and modest and carry the spirit of the ancients. You are a true friend to me."

sentences.zh: 卒，年八十餘。

translations.literal: He died at over eighty years of age.
translations.idiomatic: He died at more than eighty years of age.

sentences.zh: 子度，舉進士，至侍御史，曆京西轉運使，預修《太祖實錄》。

translations.literal: His son Du passed the jinshi examination, rose to attendant censor, served as transport commissioner of the western capital circuit, and took part in compiling the Veritable Records of Taizu.
translations.idiomatic: His son Du passed the jinshi examination, rose to the post of attendant censor, served as transport commissioner for the western capital circuit, and helped compile the Veritable Records of Emperor Taizu.

sentences.zh: 張昉有史材，曆知雜御史、省郎，至殿中少監致仕。

translations.literal: Zhang Fang had talent for historiography, served successively as supervising censor and provincial bureau secretary, and retired as vice director of the Palace Service.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Fang had a gift for historical writing. He served successively as supervising censor and secretariat officer, retired as vice director of the Palace Service, and left office.

sentences.zh: 子信，自有傳。

translations.literal: His son Xin has his own biography.
translations.idiomatic: His son Xin has a separate biography.

sentences.zh: 滕知白善為詩，至刑部員外郎、河北轉運使。

translations.literal: Teng Zhibai was skilled at poetry, rose to outer gentleman of the Ministry of Justice, and served as transport commissioner of Hebei.
translations.idiomatic: Teng Zhibai was an accomplished poet who rose to outer gentleman in the Ministry of Justice and served as transport commissioner for Hebei.

sentences.zh: 子涉，為給事中。

translations.literal: His son She served as supervising secretary.
translations.idiomatic: His son She served as supervising secretary at court.

sentences.zh: 高象先

translations.literal: Gao Xiangxian
translations.idiomatic: Gao Xiangxian

sentences.zh: 高象先父凝祐，刑部郎中，以強幹稱。

translations.literal: Gao Xiangxian's father Ningyou was a bureau director in the Ministry of Justice, renowned for forceful capability.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Xiangxian's father Ningyou served as bureau director in the Ministry of Justice and was known for his forceful administrative ability.

sentences.zh: 象先，淳化中三司戶部副使，卒於光祿少卿。

translations.literal: Xiangxian, in the Chunhua era, was vice commissioner of the Revenue Section of the Three Offices, and died in the post of vice director of the Imperial Household.
translations.idiomatic: Xiangxian served in the Chunhua era as vice commissioner of the Revenue Section of the Three Offices and died while holding the post of vice director of the Imperial Household.

sentences.zh: 郭成範

translations.literal: Guo Chengfan
translations.idiomatic: Guo Chengfan

sentences.zh: 郭成範最有文，為倉部員外郎，掌安定公書記。

translations.literal: Guo Chengfan was most accomplished in letters, served as outer gentleman of the Granary Section, and was secretary to the Duke of Anding.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Chengfan was the most gifted writer among Tongwen's students. He served as outer gentleman in the Granary Section and as secretary to the Duke of Anding.

sentences.zh: 辭疾，以司封員外郎致仕，卒。

translations.literal: He pleaded illness, retired with the rank of outer gentleman of the Seals Section, and died.
translations.idiomatic: He resigned citing illness, retired with the rank of outer gentleman in the Seals Section, and later died.

sentences.zh: 王礪事母甚謹，太平興國五年進士，至屯田郎中。

translations.literal: Wang Li was very careful in serving his mother, passed the jinshi examination in the fifth year of Taiping Xingguo, and rose to bureau director in the Directorate of Agriculture.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Li was exceptionally devoted to his mother. He passed the jinshi examination in the fifth year of the Taiping Xingguo era (980) and rose to bureau director in the Directorate of Agriculture.

sentences.zh: 子渙、瀆、淵、衝、泳。

translations.literal: His sons Huan, Du, Yuan, Chong, and Yong.
translations.idiomatic: His sons were Huan, Du, Yuan, Chong, and Yong.

sentences.zh: 渙子稷臣，瀆子堯臣，並進士及第。

translations.literal: Huan's son Jichen and Du's son Yaochen both passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: Huan's son Jichen and Du's son Yaochen both passed the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 渙子夢臣，進士出身。

translations.literal: Huan's son Mengchen was a jinshi graduate.
translations.idiomatic: Huan's son Mengchen also qualified through the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 陳摶，字圖南，亳州真源人。

translations.literal: Chen Tuan, styled Tunan, was a man of Zhenyuan in Bozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Tuan, whose style was Tunan, came from Zhenyuan in Bozhou.

sentences.zh: 始四五歲，戲渦水岸側，有青衣媼乳之，自是聰悟日益。

translations.literal: From the age of four or five, while playing on the bank of the Guo River, a woman in blue garments nursed him; from then on his intelligence grew daily.
translations.idiomatic: When he was only four or five years old, while playing on the bank of the Guo River, a woman dressed in blue nursed him. From that day his intelligence grew sharper with each passing year.

sentences.zh: 及長，讀經史百家之言，一見成誦，悉無遺忘，頗以詩名。

translations.literal: When he grew up, he read the classics, histories, and the teachings of the hundred schools; at one look he could recite, forgetting nothing, and became quite renowned for poetry.
translations.idiomatic: As he grew to adulthood he read the classics, histories, and works of the hundred schools. He could recite anything at a single reading and forget nothing, and he became well known as a poet.

sentences.zh: 後唐長興中，舉進士不第，遂不求祿仕，以山水為樂。

translations.literal: In the Changxing era of Later Tang he took the jinshi examination but did not pass, and thereafter sought no salary or office, taking mountains and streams as his delight.
translations.idiomatic: During the Changxing era of Later Tang he sat for the jinshi examination but failed. He then renounced all pursuit of office and salary and devoted himself to the pleasures of mountains and streams.

sentences.zh: 自言嘗遇孫君仿、獐皮處士二人者，高尚之人也，語摶曰：「武當山九室岩可以隱居。」

translations.literal: He said that he once met two men, Sun Junfang and the Zhangpi Recluse, men of lofty character, who told Tuan, "The Nine-Chamber Cliff of Mount Wudang is suitable for reclusion."
translations.idiomatic: He said that he once met two men of lofty character, Sun Junfang and the Zhangpi Recluse, who told him, "The Nine-Chamber Cliff on Mount Wudang is a place fit for withdrawal from the world."

sentences.zh: 摶往棲焉。

translations.literal: Tuan went and dwelt there.
translations.idiomatic: He went there and made his home.

sentences.zh: 因服氣辟穀曆二十餘年，但日飲酒數杯。

translations.literal: Thereupon he practiced ingesting qi and abstaining from grain for more than twenty years, drinking only several cups of wine each day.
translations.idiomatic: He then practiced breath cultivation and grain abstention for more than twenty years, drinking only a few cups of wine each day.

sentences.zh: 移居華山雲台觀，又止少華石室。

translations.literal: He moved his dwelling to the Yuntai Abbey on Mount Hua and also stayed in the stone chamber on Lesser Hua.
translations.idiomatic: He moved to the Yuntai Abbey on Mount Hua and also stayed in a stone chamber on Lesser Hua.

sentences.zh: 每寢處，多百餘日不起。

translations.literal: Whenever he slept, he often did not rise for more than a hundred days.
translations.idiomatic: When he slept, he would often remain in slumber for more than a hundred days at a stretch.

sentences.zh: 周世宗好黃白術，有以摶名聞者，顯德三年，命華州送至闕下。

translations.literal: Emperor Shizong of Zhou loved the arts of gold and elixir; someone who had heard of Tuan's fame reported it, and in the third year of Xiande he ordered Hua Prefecture to send him to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shizong of Zhou was devoted to alchemical arts of gold and elixir. When Tuan's reputation reached the court, in the third year of the Xiande era (956) the emperor ordered the authorities of Hua Prefecture to escort him to the capital.

sentences.zh: 留止禁中月餘，從容問其術，摶對曰：「陛下為四海之主，當以致治為念，奈何留意黃白之事乎？」

translations.literal: He was detained in the inner palace for more than a month; the emperor at leisure asked about his arts, and Tuan replied, "Your Majesty is lord of the four seas—you should take bringing order as your concern; why fix your mind on matters of gold and elixir?"
translations.idiomatic: He was kept in the inner palace for more than a month. The emperor questioned him at leisure about his arts, and Tuan replied, "Your Majesty is sovereign of the four seas. You ought to devote yourself to bringing order to the realm. Why concern yourself with alchemical gold and elixir?"

sentences.zh: 世宗不之責，命為諫議大夫，固辭不受。

translations.literal: Shizong did not blame him, appointed him remonstrance and policy grandee, but he firmly declined and did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: Shizong did not reproach him. He offered Tuan the post of remonstrance and policy grandee, but Tuan firmly declined.

sentences.zh: 既知其無他術，放還所止，詔本州長吏歲時存問。

translations.literal: Once it was known that he had no other arts, he was released to his dwelling; an edict ordered the prefectural chief officials to visit and inquire of him at the seasons.
translations.idiomatic: Once the court realized he possessed no other arts, he was sent back to his mountain retreat. An edict instructed the prefectural officials to visit and inquire after him at the proper seasons.

sentences.zh: 五年，成州刺史朱憲陛辭赴任，世宗令齎帛五十匹、茶三十斤賜摶。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, Zhu Xian, prefect of Chengzhou, took leave at court before proceeding to his post; Shizong ordered him to carry fifty bolts of silk and thirty jin of tea as gifts for Tuan.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year (958), Zhu Xian, prefect of Chengzhou, took his leave at court before departing for his post. Shizong instructed him to bring fifty bolts of silk and thirty jin of tea as gifts for Tuan.

sentences.zh: 太平興國中來朝，太宗待之甚厚。

translations.literal: During Taiping Xingguo he came to court; Taizong treated him with great generosity.
translations.idiomatic: During the Taiping Xingguo era he came to court, and Emperor Taizong received him with exceptional generosity.

sentences.zh: 九年復來朝，上益加禮重，謂宰相宋琪等曰：「摶獨善其身，不幹勢利，所謂方外之士也。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he came to court again; the emperor increased his courtesy still more and said to the chief ministers Song Qi and others, "Tuan cultivates himself alone and does not meddle in power and profit—he is what is called a man beyond the world.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year (984) he came to court again. The emperor treated him with still greater honor and told the chief ministers Song Qi and others, "Tuan keeps to himself and never meddles in power or profit. He is truly a man of the world beyond the court.

sentences.zh: 摶居華山已四十餘年，度其年近百歲。

translations.literal: Tuan had dwelt on Mount Hua for more than forty years; it was estimated that his age was nearly a hundred.
translations.idiomatic: Tuan had lived on Mount Hua for more than forty years, and it was thought that he was nearing a hundred years of age.

sentences.zh: 自言經承五代離亂，幸天下太平，故來朝覲。

translations.literal: He said himself that he had lived through the disorders and separations of the Five Dynasties and, fortunate in the empire's peace, therefore came to pay court.
translations.idiomatic: He explained that he had lived through the chaos and division of the Five Dynasties and, now that the realm was at peace, had come to pay his respects at court.

sentences.zh: 與之語，甚可聽。」

translations.literal: Conversation with him was very worth hearing."
translations.idiomatic: His conversation was most engaging to hear."

sentences.zh: 因遣中使送至中書，琪等從容問曰：「先生得玄默修養之道，可以教人乎？」

translations.literal: Thereupon he sent a palace envoy to escort him to the Secretariat; Qi and the others at leisure asked, "Has the master obtained the Way of mysterious silence and cultivation—can you teach others?"
translations.idiomatic: He then sent a palace envoy to escort Tuan to the Secretariat. Qi and the others questioned him at leisure: "Have you mastered the Way of silent cultivation? Can you teach it to others?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「摶山野之人，於時無用，亦不知神仙黃白之事，吐納養生之理，非有方術可傳。

translations.literal: He replied, "Tuan is a man of mountains and wilds, of no use to the age, and also does not know the affairs of immortals and gold and elixir, or the principles of exhalation-inhalation and nurturing life—there are no methods that can be transmitted.
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "I am only a man of the mountains and wilds, of no use to the age. I know nothing of immortals or alchemical gold and elixir, nor of the principles of breath cultivation and nurturing life. There is no art I can pass on.

sentences.zh: 假令白日衝天，亦何益於世？

translations.literal: Even if one soared to heaven in broad daylight, what benefit would it be to the world?
translations.idiomatic: Even if one were to ascend to heaven in broad daylight, what good would that do the world?

sentences.zh: 今聖上龍顏秀異，有天人之表，博達古今，深究治亂，真有道仁聖之主也。

translations.literal: Now the sage sovereign's dragon countenance is outstanding and unusual, with the bearing of heaven and man; broadly penetrating past and present, deeply investigating order and disorder—he is truly a lord of the Way, benevolence, and sagacity.
translations.idiomatic: The present sage sovereign has a noble and extraordinary countenance, the bearing of one who unites heaven and humanity. He is broadly learned in past and present and probes deeply into the causes of order and chaos. He is truly a ruler of the Way, benevolence, and sagely wisdom.

sentences.zh: 正君臣協心同德、興化致治之秋，勤行修煉，無出於此。」

translations.literal: It is just the season when ruler and ministers unite in heart and virtue to raise transformation and bring order—diligent cultivation has nothing beyond this."
translations.idiomatic: This is the season when ruler and ministers should unite in heart and virtue to raise the realm and bring about good government. There is no cultivation more worth pursuing than this."

sentences.zh: 琪等稱善，以其語白上。

translations.literal: Qi and the others praised it as good and reported his words to the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Qi and the others praised his words and reported them to the emperor.

sentences.zh: 上益重之，下詔賜號希夷先生，仍賜紫衣一襲，留摶闕下，令有司增葺所止雲台觀。

translations.literal: The emperor esteemed him still more, issued an edict granting him the title Master Rarefied-Stillness, and also bestowed a set of purple robes; he kept Tuan at the capital and ordered the relevant offices to enlarge and repair the Yuntai Abbey where he dwelt.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor held him in still greater esteem, issued an edict granting him the title Master Rarefied Stillness, and bestowed a set of purple robes. He kept Tuan at the capital and ordered the authorities to enlarge and repair the Yuntai Abbey on Mount Hua where Tuan lived.

sentences.zh: 上屢與之屬和詩賦，數月放還山。

translations.literal: The emperor repeatedly exchanged matching poems and rhapsodies with him; after several months he was released back to the mountains.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor often exchanged matching poems and rhapsodies with him. After several months he was allowed to return to his mountain retreat.

sentences.zh: 端拱初，忽謂弟子賈德升曰：「汝可於張超穀鑿石為室，吾將憩焉。」

translations.literal: At the beginning of Duangong he suddenly said to his disciple Jia Desheng, "You may carve a stone chamber in Zhangchao Valley; I shall rest there."
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Duangong era (988) he suddenly told his disciple Jia Desheng, "Carve a stone chamber for me in Zhangchao Valley. I shall rest there."

sentences.zh: 二年秋七月，石室成，摶手書數百言為表，其略曰：「臣摶大數有終，聖朝難戀，已於今月二十二日化形於蓮花峰下張超穀中。」

translations.literal: In the seventh month of autumn of the second year the stone chamber was completed; Tuan wrote several hundred characters by hand as a memorial, the gist of which was: "Your subject Tuan's great number has an end; the sage court is hard to linger in—I have already on the twenty-second of this month transformed my form in Zhangchao Valley below Lotus Peak."
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of autumn of the second year (989) the stone chamber was finished. Tuan wrote a memorial of several hundred characters in his own hand, which in essence read: "Your subject Tuan's allotted span has reached its end, and the sage court is hard to linger in. On the twenty-second of this month I have already transformed my form in Zhangchao Valley below Lotus Peak."

sentences.zh: 如期而卒，經七日支體猶溫。

translations.literal: He died on the appointed day; after seven days his limbs were still warm.
translations.idiomatic: He died on the appointed day. Seven days later his body was still warm to the touch.

sentences.zh: 有五色雲蔽塞洞口，彌月不散。

translations.literal: There were five-colored clouds covering and blocking the cave mouth, not dispersing for a full month.
translations.idiomatic: Five-colored clouds covered the mouth of the cave and did not disperse for an entire month.

sentences.zh: 摶好讀《易》，手不釋卷。

translations.literal: Tuan loved to read the Changes and never let the scroll leave his hand.
translations.idiomatic: Tuan loved to read the Book of Changes and never let the scroll leave his hand.

sentences.zh: 常自號扶搖子，著《指玄篇》八十一章，言導養及還丹之事。

translations.literal: He often styled himself Master Fuyao and composed eighty-one chapters of Pointing to the Mysterious, treating guiding nourishment and returning the elixir.
translations.idiomatic: He often called himself Master Fuyao and wrote eighty-one chapters of Pointing to the Mysterious, on the arts of nurturing life and restoring the elixir.

sentences.zh: 宰相王溥亦著八十一章以箋其指。

translations.literal: Chief Minister Wang Pu also wrote eighty-one chapters as commentary on its meaning.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Minister Wang Pu also wrote eighty-one chapters commenting on its meaning.

sentences.zh: 摶又有《三峰寓言》及《高陽集》、《釣潭集》，詩六百餘首。

translations.literal: Tuan also had Fables of the Three Peaks and the collections Gaoyang ji and Diaotan ji, more than six hundred poems.
translations.idiomatic: Tuan also wrote Fables of the Three Peaks and the collections Collected Works from Gaoyang and Collected Works from Diaotan, comprising more than six hundred poems.

sentences.zh: 能逆知人意，齋中有大瓢掛壁上，道士賈休復心欲之，摶已知其意，謂休復曰：「子來非有他，蓋欲吾瓢爾。」

translations.literal: He could know others' intentions in advance; in his study a large gourd hung on the wall. The Daoist Jia Xiufu desired it in his heart; Tuan already knew his intent and said to Xiufu, "You have come for no other reason—you want my gourd."
translations.idiomatic: He could read people's intentions before they spoke. A large gourd hung on the wall of his study. The Daoist priest Jia Xiufu coveted it, but Tuan had already perceived his wish and said, "You have come for no other reason—you want my gourd."

sentences.zh: 呼侍者取以與之，休復大驚，以為神。

translations.literal: He called a servant to take it down and give it to him; Xiufu was greatly startled and regarded him as divine.
translations.idiomatic: He called a servant to take it down and give it to him. Xiufu was astonished and took him for a supernatural being.

sentences.zh: 有郭沆者，少居華陰，夜宿雲台觀。

translations.literal: There was a Guo Kang who in youth lived in Huayin and one night lodged at the Yuntai Abbey.
translations.idiomatic: There was a man named Guo Kang who had lived in Huayin since youth. One night he stayed at the Yuntai Abbey.

sentences.zh: 摶中夜呼令趣歸，沆未決；

translations.literal: Tuan in the middle of the night called for him to hurry home; Kang had not yet decided;
translations.idiomatic: In the middle of the night Tuan called for him to hurry home, but Kang hesitated;

sentences.zh: 有頃，復日曰：「可勿歸矣。」

translations.literal: after a while he again said, "You need not return now."
translations.idiomatic: after a moment he said again, "You need not go home now."

sentences.zh: 明日，沆還家，果中夜母暴得心痛幾死，食頃而愈。

translations.literal: The next day Kang returned home; indeed in the middle of the night his mother had suddenly suffered heart pain and nearly died, recovering after the time it takes to eat a meal.
translations.idiomatic: The next day Kang went home and found that in the middle of the night his mother had suddenly been stricken with heart pain and nearly died, recovering only after the time it takes to eat a meal.

sentences.zh: 華陰隱士李琪，自言唐開元中郎官，已數百歲，人罕見者；

translations.literal: the Huayin recluse Li Qi, who said himself that he had been a court gentleman in the Kaiyuan era of Tang, was already several hundred years old and rarely seen by people;
translations.idiomatic: The Huayin recluse Li Qi claimed to have been a court gentleman in the Kaiyuan era of Tang and to be already several hundred years old. Few people ever saw him;

sentences.zh: 關西逸人呂洞賓有劍術，百餘歲而童顏，步履輕疾，頃刻數百里，世以為神仙。

translations.literal: the Guanxi free man Lü Dongbin had sword arts, was over a hundred years old with a child's face, walked lightly and swiftly, covering several hundred li in an instant—the world took him for an immortal.
translations.idiomatic: and the Guanxi free man Lü Dongbin, master of the sword, was over a hundred years old yet had the face of a child. He walked lightly and swiftly and could cover several hundred li in an instant. The world regarded him as an immortal.

sentences.zh: 皆數來摶齋中，人咸異之。

translations.literal: All several times came to Tuan's study; people all marveled at it.
translations.idiomatic: All of them visited Tuan's study repeatedly, and everyone who heard of it was astonished.

sentences.zh: 大中祥符四年，真宗幸華陰，至雲台觀，閱摶畫像，除其觀田租。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Dazhong Xiangfu, Zhenzong visited Huayin, came to the Yuntai Abbey, viewed Tuan's portrait, and remitted the abbey's field rent.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of the Dazhong Xiangfu era (1011), Emperor Zhenzong visited Huayin, went to the Yuntai Abbey, viewed Tuan's portrait, and remitted the abbey's land tax.

sentences.zh: 又有許瓊者，開封鄢陵人。

translations.literal: There was also a Xu Qiong, a man of Yanling in Kaifeng.
translations.idiomatic: There was also a man named Xu Qiong from Yanling in Kaifeng.

sentences.zh: 開寶五年，子永罷盧縣尉，詣匭上言：「臣年七十五，父瓊年九十九，長兄年八十一，次兄年七十九，欲乞近地一官，以就榮養。」

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Kaibao, his son Yong left the post of county lieutenant of Lu and went to the suggestion box to say, "Your subject is seventy-five; Father Qiong is ninety-nine; the eldest brother is eighty-one and the second brother seventy-nine. I wish to beg a nearby office in order to honor and support them."
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of the Kaibao era (972), his son Yong left his post as county lieutenant of Lu and submitted a petition to the suggestion box: "Your subject is seventy-five years old. My father Qiong is ninety-nine. My eldest brother is eighty-one and my second brother seventy-nine. I beg a nearby office so that I may honor and support them."

sentences.zh: 上覽奏，召永訊之，即命迎其父赴闕。

translations.literal: The emperor read the memorial, summoned Yong to question him, and at once ordered his father brought to court.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor read the memorial, summoned Yong for questioning, and immediately ordered his father brought to the capital.

sentences.zh: 瓊得對於講武殿，上顧問久之，悉能奏對，而詞氣不衰，言唐末以來事，曆曆可聽。

translations.literal: Qiong was granted audience in the Hall of Martial Instruction; the emperor questioned him at length, and he could answer everything; his tone did not flag, and when he spoke of affairs from the end of Tang onward, each point was worth hearing.
translations.idiomatic: Qiong was granted an audience in the Hall of Martial Instruction. The emperor questioned him at length, and he answered every question without faltering. When he spoke of events from the end of the Tang onward, each detail was vivid and worth hearing.

sentences.zh: 上悅其父子俱享遐壽，賜襲衣、犀帶、銀鞍勒馬、帛三十匹、茶二十斤，授永鄢城令。

translations.literal: The emperor rejoiced that father and son both enjoyed long life, bestowed court robes, rhinoceros-horn belt, silver saddle and bridle, horse, thirty bolts of silk, and twenty jin of tea, and appointed Yong magistrate of Yancheng.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was pleased that father and son both enjoyed such long life. He bestowed court robes, a rhinoceros-horn belt, a silver saddle and bridle, a horse, thirty bolts of silk, and twenty jin of tea, and appointed Yong magistrate of Yancheng.

sentences.zh: 是時，澶密齊沂、萊江吉萬州、江陰梁山軍，各奏八十已上呂繼美等二十九人，並賜爵公士。

translations.literal: At that time, Cao, Mi, Qi, Yi, Lai, Jiang, Ji, Wan, Jiangyin, and Liangshan Army each reported twenty-nine persons aged eighty and above, such as Lü Jimei, and all were granted the noble rank of gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the prefectures of Cao, Mi, Qi, Yi, Lai, Jiang, Ji, and Wan, together with Jiangyin and Liangshan Army, each reported twenty-nine men aged eighty or above, including Lü Jimei, and all were granted the honorary rank of gentleman.

sentences.zh: 真宗時，凡老人年百歲已上者，州縣以名聞，皆詔賜衣帛、米麥，長吏存撫之。

translations.literal: In Zhenzong's time, whenever an old person was a hundred years or more, the prefecture and county reported the name; all were ordered gifts of robes, silk, rice, and wheat, and the chief officials visited and comforted them.
translations.idiomatic: During the reign of Zhenzong, whenever an elderly person reached a hundred years of age, the local authorities reported the name to the court. An edict always granted robes, silk, rice, and wheat, and the chief officials were instructed to visit and comfort them.

sentences.zh: 种放，字明逸，河南洛陽人也。

translations.literal: Zhong Fang, styled Mingyi, was a man of Luoyang in Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong Fang, whose style was Mingyi, came from Luoyang in Henan.

sentences.zh: 父詡，吏部令史，調補長安主簿。

translations.literal: His father Xu was a clerk in the Ministry of Personnel and was transferred to fill the post of registrar of Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: His father Xu served as a clerk in the Ministry of Personnel and was transferred to the post of registrar of Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 放沉默好學，七歲能屬文，不與群兒戲。

translations.literal: Fang was silent and loved learning; at seven he could compose literary pieces and did not play with the crowd of children.
translations.idiomatic: Fang was quiet and devoted to learning. At seven he could compose literary pieces and never joined in children's games.

sentences.zh: 父嘗令舉進士，放辭以業未成，不可妄動。

translations.literal: His father once ordered him to take the jinshi examination; Fang declined on the ground that his studies were not yet complete and one must not act rashly.
translations.idiomatic: His father once urged him to sit for the jinshi examination, but Fang declined, saying his studies were not yet complete and one must not act rashly.

sentences.zh: 每往來嵩、華間，慨然有山林意。

translations.literal: Whenever he traveled between Song and Hua, he sighed with the intent of mountains and forests.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he traveled between Mount Song and Mount Hua, he was moved by a longing for life in the mountains and forests.

sentences.zh: 未幾父卒，數兄皆幹進，獨放與母俱隱終南豹林穀之東明峰，結草為廬，僅庇風雨。

translations.literal: Before long his father died; several elder brothers all sought advancement, but Fang alone with his mother withdrew to Dongming Peak in Baolin Valley of the Zhongnan range, making a hut of grass that barely sheltered from wind and rain.
translations.idiomatic: Before long his father died. Several elder brothers all pursued official careers, but Fang alone withdrew with his mother to Dongming Peak in Baolin Valley on the Zhongnan range. They built a grass hut that barely kept out wind and rain.

sentences.zh: 以講習為業，從學者眾，得束脩以養母，母亦樂道，薄滋味。

translations.literal: He took lecturing and study as his occupation; many followed to learn; he received bundles of dried meat to support his mother; his mother also delighted in the Way and was sparing in flavors.
translations.idiomatic: He made teaching his livelihood. Many students came to study with him, and the gifts he received supported his mother. His mother also delighted in the Way and lived on plain food.

sentences.zh: 放得辟穀術，別為堂於峰頂，盡日望雲危坐。

translations.literal: Fang obtained the art of grain abstention and built a separate hall on the peak summit, sitting upright all day gazing at the clouds.
translations.idiomatic: Fang mastered the art of grain abstention and built a separate hall on the summit of the peak, where he sat upright all day gazing at the clouds.

sentences.zh: 每山水暴漲，道路阻隔，糧糗乏絕，止食芋栗。

translations.literal: Whenever mountain floods rose violently, roads were cut off, and provisions ran out, he ate only taro and chestnuts.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever mountain floods cut off the roads and provisions ran out, he ate only taro and chestnuts.

sentences.zh: 性嗜酒，嘗種秫自釀，每曰空山清寂，聊以養和，因號雲溪醉侯。

translations.literal: By nature he loved wine; he once planted glutinous millet and brewed it himself, saying each time that in the empty mountains' clarity and silence he might for a while nurture harmony, and therefore styled himself the Cloud-Stream Drunken Marquis.
translations.idiomatic: He loved wine by nature. He planted glutinous millet and brewed his own, remarking that in the silent clarity of the empty mountains he could nurture his harmony, and so he took the sobriquet Cloud-Stream Drunken Marquis.

sentences.zh: 幅巾短褐，負琴攜壺，溯長溪，坐磐石，采山藥以助飲，往往終日。

translations.literal: In cloth headcloth and short hemp robe, carrying a zither and bringing a wine jar, he went up the long stream, sat on boulder rocks, gathered mountain herbs to aid his drinking, and often passed the whole day thus.
translations.idiomatic: Dressed in a cloth cap and short hemp robe, he would carry his zither and wine jar upstream along the long creek, sit on boulders, gather mountain herbs to season his drink, and often pass the entire day that way.

sentences.zh: 值月夕或至宵分，自豹林抵州郭七十里，徒步與樵人往返。

translations.literal: On moonlit evenings, sometimes until midnight, from Baolin to the prefectural town was seventy li; he went on foot back and forth with woodcutters.
translations.idiomatic: On moonlit nights, sometimes until midnight, he would walk the seventy li from Baolin to the prefectural town on foot, going back and forth among the woodcutters.

sentences.zh: 性不喜浮圖氏，嘗裂佛經以製帷帳。

translations.literal: By nature he did not like the Buddhist school; he once tore Buddhist sutras to make curtains.
translations.idiomatic: He disliked Buddhism by nature and once tore Buddhist sutras to make curtains.

sentences.zh: 所著《蒙書》十卷及《嗣禹說》、《表孟子上下篇》、《太一祠錄》，人頗稱之。

translations.literal: His works included ten scrolls of the Book of Instruction, Succession to Yu's Discourse, Petition on the Upper and Lower Chapters of Mencius, and Record of the Grand Unity Shrine—people praised them considerably.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote ten scrolls of the Book of Instruction, Succession to Yu's Discourse, Petition on the Upper and Lower Chapters of Mencius, and Record of the Grand Unity Shrine, all of which won considerable praise.

sentences.zh: 多為歌詩，自稱「退士」，嘗作傳以述其志。

translations.literal: He composed many songs and poems, styled himself "the Retired Gentleman," and once wrote a biography to set forth his aims.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote many songs and poems, called himself "the Retired Gentleman," and once composed a biography setting forth his aims.

sentences.zh: 四年，兵部尚書張齊賢言放隱居三十年，不遊城市十五載，孝行純至，可勵風俗，簡樸退靜，無謝古人。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, Minister of War Zhang Qixian said that Fang had lived in reclusion thirty years, not visited cities for fifteen years, his filial conduct was pure and utmost, able to encourage custom, simple and retiring in quiet—no shame before the ancients.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year, Minister of War Zhang Qixian reported that Fang had lived in seclusion for thirty years and had not visited a city for fifteen. His filial conduct was pure and exemplary, his manner simple and retiring—he was in no way inferior to the ancients and could serve to encourage public morals.

sentences.zh: 復詔本府遣官詣山，以禮發遣赴闕，齎裝錢五萬，放辭不起。

translations.literal: Again an edict ordered the prefecture to send an official to the mountain to escort him with ceremony to court, carrying fifty thousand in travel funds; Fang declined and did not rise.
translations.idiomatic: An edict again ordered the prefecture to send an official to the mountain to escort him respectfully to court with fifty thousand in travel funds. Fang declined and would not go.

sentences.zh: 明年，齊賢出守京兆，復條陳放操行，請加旌賁。

translations.literal: The next year Qixian went out to guard the capital district and again itemized Fang's conduct, requesting added honors.
translations.idiomatic: The following year Qixian took up his post as governor of the capital district and again submitted a detailed account of Fang's conduct, requesting that he receive further honors.

sentences.zh: 即賜詔曰：「汝隱居丘園，博通今古，孝悌之行，鄉里所推，慕古人之遺榮，挹君子之常道。

translations.literal: An edict was at once granted saying, "You dwell in reclusion in hill and garden, are broadly versed in past and present, your conduct of filial piety and brotherly duty is what the village commends, you admire the ancients' leaving glory behind, and draw up the noble person's constant Way.
translations.idiomatic: An edict was immediately issued: "You dwell in seclusion among hills and gardens, are broadly learned in past and present, and your filial and brotherly conduct is praised throughout your neighborhood. You admire the ancients who renounced worldly glory and embrace the noble person's constant Way.

sentences.zh: 屢覽守藩之奏，彌彰遁世之風，載渴來儀，副予延佇。

translations.literal: Repeatedly reading the memorials of border guardians, your manner of withdrawing from the world shines ever more; I thirst for your coming—meet my long waiting.
translations.idiomatic: I have read repeatedly the memorials of regional governors praising your withdrawal from the world. I long for your coming and hope you will answer my earnest expectation.

sentences.zh: 今遣供奉官周旺齎詔，召汝赴闕，賜帛百匹、錢十萬。」

translations.literal: Now I send the palace attendant Zhou Wang bearing the edict to summon you to court and bestow one hundred bolts of silk and one hundred thousand cash."
translations.idiomatic: I now send the palace attendant Zhou Wang with this edict to summon you to court and bestow one hundred bolts of silk and one hundred thousand cash."

sentences.zh: 九月，放至，對崇政殿，以幅巾見，命坐與語，詢以民政邊事。

translations.literal: In the ninth month Fang arrived, had audience in the Hall of Esteeming Governance, appeared in cloth headcloth, was ordered to sit and converse, and was questioned on civil administration and frontier affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month Fang arrived and was received in the Hall of Esteeming Governance. He appeared wearing a plain cloth cap, was invited to sit and converse, and was questioned on civil administration and frontier affairs.

sentences.zh: 放曰：「明王之治，愛民而已，惟徐而化之。」

translations.literal: Fang said, "The enlightened king's governance is nothing but loving the people—only gradually transforming them."
translations.idiomatic: Fang said, "The governance of an enlightened king consists in loving the people and transforming them only gradually."

sentences.zh: 餘皆謙讓不對。

translations.literal: On the rest he was modest and declined to answer.
translations.idiomatic: On all other questions he modestly declined to reply.

sentences.zh: 即日授左司諫、直昭文館，賜巾服簡帶，館於都亭驛，大官供膳。

translations.literal: That same day he was appointed left remonstrance bureau censor and concurrent scholar of the Hall for the Illustrious of Culture, granted headcloth, robes, and bamboo tally, lodged at the Capital Pavilion Station, with the imperial kitchen supplying meals.
translations.idiomatic: That same day he was appointed left remonstrance bureau censor and concurrent scholar of the Hall for the Illustrious of Culture. He was granted official cap, robes, and tally, lodged at the Capital Pavilion Station, and supplied with meals from the imperial kitchen.

sentences.zh: 翌日，表辭恩命。

translations.literal: The next day he submitted a memorial declining the gracious appointment.
translations.idiomatic: The next day he submitted a memorial declining the appointment.

sentences.zh: 上知放舊與陳堯叟遊，令堯叟諭意；

translations.literal: The emperor knew Fang had formerly been friendly with Chen Yaosou and ordered Yaosou to convey his intent;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor knew Fang had once been close to Chen Yaosou and ordered Yaosou to convey his wishes;

sentences.zh: 又謂宰相曰：「朕求茂異，以廣視聽，資治道。

translations.literal: he also said to the chief ministers, "I seek outstanding talent to broaden sight and hearing and supply the way of governance.
translations.idiomatic: he also told the chief ministers, "I seek outstanding talent to broaden my understanding and aid the way of governance.

sentences.zh: 如放終未樂仁，亦可遂其請也。」

translations.literal: If Fang in the end is not pleased with benevolence, his request may also be granted."
translations.idiomatic: If Fang in the end is not willing to serve, his request may also be granted."

sentences.zh: 中書傳詔，放曰：「病居山林，天恩累加禮聘，岩猿溪鳥之性，固不敢以祿仕為意。

translations.literal: The Secretariat transmitted the edict; Fang said, "Ill, dwelling in mountains and forests, heaven's grace repeatedly adding ceremonial summons—the nature of cliff apes and stream birds—how could I dare take salary and office as my intent?
translations.idiomatic: The Secretariat conveyed the edict. Fang replied, "Ill and dwelling in the mountains and forests, I have received heaven's grace in repeated ceremonial summons. I have the nature of cliff apes and stream birds and would never dare to seek salary and office.

sentences.zh: 然主上虛懷待士，旰食憂人之心，亦不敢以羈束為念。」

translations.literal: Yet the sovereign's open mind in treating scholars and his heart of eating late and worrying for the people—I also dare not think of restraint as my concern."
translations.idiomatic: Yet the sovereign receives scholars with an open mind and worries for the people even at his meals. I also dare not think only of being bound by office."

sentences.zh: 遂詔不聽其讓。

translations.literal: Thereupon an edict did not accept his declination.
translations.idiomatic: An edict was issued refusing to accept his resignation.

sentences.zh: 數日，復召見，賜緋衣、象簡、犀帶、銀魚，御製五言詩寵之，賜昭慶坊第一區，加帷帳什物，銀器五百兩，錢三十萬。

translations.literal: Several days later he was again summoned; he was granted crimson robes, ivory tally, rhinoceros belt, and silver fish; the emperor composed a five-character poem to honor him; he was given the foremost residence in Zhaoping Ward, added curtains and furnishings, five hundred taels of silver vessels, and three hundred thousand cash.
translations.idiomatic: Several days later he was summoned again and granted crimson robes, an ivory tally, a rhinoceros-horn belt, and a silver fish badge. The emperor composed a five-character poem in his honor and gave him the finest residence in Zhaoping Ward, along with curtains, furnishings, five hundred taels of silver vessels, and three hundred thousand cash.

sentences.zh: 中謝日，賜食學士院，自是屢得召對。

translations.literal: On the day of his thanksgiving audience he was granted a meal at the Academy of Scholars; from then on he was repeatedly summoned to audience.
translations.idiomatic: On the day he expressed his thanks he was entertained at the Academy of Scholars. From then on he was repeatedly summoned to audience.

sentences.zh: 六年春，再表謝暫歸故山，詔許其請。

translations.literal: In the spring of the sixth year he again memorialized thanks and asked to return temporarily to his old mountain; an edict granted his request.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the sixth year he again submitted a memorial asking to return temporarily to his mountain home. An edict granted his request.

sentences.zh: 將行，又遷起居舍人，命館閣官宴餞於瓊林苑，上賜七言詩三章，在席皆賦。

translations.literal: As he was about to depart he was further promoted to diarist; palace and academy officials were ordered to give a farewell banquet in the Qionglin Garden; the emperor bestowed three seven-character poems, and all present composed verses.
translations.idiomatic: As he was about to depart he was promoted to diarist. Palace and academy officials were ordered to give him a farewell banquet in the Qionglin Garden. The emperor bestowed three seven-character poems, and everyone present composed verses in reply.

sentences.zh: 十月，遣使就山撫問，圖其林泉居處以獻，優詔趣其入覲，放以疾未平為請。

translations.literal: In the tenth month an envoy was sent to the mountain to comfort and inquire; his forest-and-stream dwelling was painted and presented; a gracious edict urged him to come to audience; Fang pleaded that his illness was not yet settled.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month an envoy was sent to his mountain retreat to inquire after him. A painting of his forest dwelling was presented to the court. A gracious edict urged him to return to audience, but Fang pleaded that his illness had not yet subsided.

sentences.zh: 放山居草舍五六區，啖野蔬蕎麥。

translations.literal: Fang's mountain dwelling had five or six grass huts; he ate wild vegetables, buckwheat, and millet.
translations.idiomatic: Fang's mountain home consisted of five or six grass huts. He lived on wild vegetables, buckwheat, and millet.

sentences.zh: 表求太宗御書及經史音疏，悉給焉。

translations.literal: He memorialized requesting Taizong's imperial calligraphy and phonological commentaries on the classics and histories; all were granted.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized requesting Taizong's imperial calligraphy and phonological commentaries on the classics and histories, and all were granted.

sentences.zh: 十月，復至，上謂宰相曰：「放比來高尚其事，每所詢問，頗有可采。

translations.literal: In the tenth month he came again; the emperor said to the chief ministers, "Fang of late has elevated his affairs; in each inquiry there is much worth adopting.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month he returned. The emperor told the chief ministers, "Fang of late has conducted himself with lofty integrity, and in each consultation there is much worth adopting.

sentences.zh: 朝廷雖加爵秩，而未能大用，即物議未厭，所慮放卷而懷之。」

translations.literal: Though the court has added rank and title, he has not yet been greatly employed—that is, public discussion is not yet satisfied; what is feared is that Fang, though yielding, harbors resentment in his heart."
translations.idiomatic: Although the court has granted him rank and title, he has not yet been given a major post, and public opinion is not yet satisfied. What is feared is that Fang, though outwardly yielding, may harbor resentment in his heart."

sentences.zh: 即遣內侍任文慶齎詔諭之曰：「朕臨御寰區，憂勤旰昃，詳延茂異，物色隱淪，思訪話言，用熙庶績。

translations.literal: He at once sent the inner attendant Ren Wenqing bearing an edict to instruct him, saying, "I face and rule the realm, anxious and diligent until sunset, broadly extending to outstanding talent, seeking out the hidden and submerged, thinking to visit and hear words, to employ them for the flourishing of the multitude's achievements.
translations.idiomatic: He immediately sent the palace attendant Ren Wenqing with an edict instructing him: "I rule the realm with anxious diligence even at sunset, broadly seeking outstanding talent and searching out those hidden from public life, eager to hear their counsel and employ it for the flourishing of the realm.

sentences.zh: 以卿棲心岩竇，屏跡囂塵，躡綺皓之遐蹤，有曾、顏之至行，特舉賁園之典，果符前席之心。

translations.literal: Because you lodge your heart in cliff caves, screen your traces from dusty clamor, tread the far footprints of Qi and Hao, possess the utmost conduct of Zeng and Yan—you were specially raised by the ceremony of the Honored Garden, and it truly matched the heart of moving forward the mat.
translations.idiomatic: Because you lodge your heart in mountain caves, keep your distance from the dust of the world, follow the distant footsteps of the recluses Qi and Hao, and possess the supreme conduct of Zeng and Yan, I specially honored you with the ceremony of the Honored Garden, and your coming truly answered my earnest wish.

sentences.zh: 每所諮詢，備詳理道，載觀敷納，蔚有材謀，深簡朕懷，頗思大用。

translations.literal: In each consultation you are fully detailed in principle and the Way; observing your presentations and acceptances, you abundantly have talent and planning—deeply meeting my heart, I quite think to employ you greatly.
translations.idiomatic: In each consultation you are thorough in principle and the Way. Observing your presentations, I see abundant talent and counsel that deeply meets my expectations, and I am inclined to employ you in a major capacity.

sentences.zh: 然以群情未悉，成命是稽。

translations.literal: Yet because the multitude's feelings are not yet informed, the completed command is deferred.
translations.idiomatic: Yet because public opinion is not yet fully persuaded, the final appointment has been deferred.

sentences.zh: 今四隩來同，萬區思乂，方崇政本，庶厚時風。

translations.literal: Now the four corners come together, the myriad regions think of governance; we are just exalting the root of government, hoping to thicken the customs of the age.
translations.idiomatic: Now the four corners of the realm are united and the myriad regions yearn for good government. We are exalting the foundations of rule and hope to improve the customs of the age.

sentences.zh: 卿必能酌斟化源，丹青王度，恢富國強兵之術，陳制禮作樂之規。

translations.literal: You surely can measure the source of transformation, plan the king's measure, expand the arts of enriching the state and strengthening the army, and set forth regulations for establishing rites and composing music.
translations.idiomatic: You surely can discern the source of transformation, delineate the royal standard, expand the arts of enriching the state and strengthening the army, and set forth regulations for establishing rites and composing music.

sentences.zh: 返樸還淳，措刑息訟，輔予不逮，馴至太平，登用機衡，弼成寡昧。

translations.literal: Return simplicity and restore purity, set aside punishments and still lawsuits, assist my inadequacies, gradually reach great peace, ascend to the pivots and balances, and help complete my few dimnesses.
translations.idiomatic: Restore simplicity and purity, set punishments aside and still lawsuits, assist my inadequacies, gradually bring about great peace, take up the pivots of state, and help complete what my limited wisdom cannot achieve.

sentences.zh: 卿宜體茲眷遇，罄乃誠明，敘經國之大猷，述致君之遠略，盡形奏牘，以沃朕心。

translations.literal: You should embody this gracious encounter, exhaust your sincerity and clarity, narrate the great plans for ordering the state, relate the far-reaching strategies for serving the ruler, fully set them forth in memorials, to enrich my heart.
translations.idiomatic: You should respond to this gracious favor with full sincerity, set forth the great plans for ordering the state, relate the far-reaching strategies for serving the ruler, and lay them all out in memorials to enrich my understanding.

sentences.zh: 副涼德之倚毗，褰外朝之觀聽，乃司樞務，式洽至公。」

translations.literal: Assist my modest virtue's reliance and support, draw aside the outer court's observation and hearing, then preside over pivotal affairs, and thereby accord with utmost fairness."
translations.idiomatic: Assist my modest virtue, answer the scrutiny of the outer court, preside over pivotal affairs of state, and thereby accord with utmost fairness."

sentences.zh: 放上言曰：「臣讀書業文，實自父師之誨，學古嗜退，本求山水之樂。

translations.literal: Fang submitted saying, "Your subject's reading books and pursuing letters truly came from father and teacher's instruction; studying antiquity and loving withdrawal, originally sought the joy of mountains and waters.
translations.idiomatic: Fang submitted a memorial saying, "Your subject's study of books and pursuit of letters came truly from the instruction of father and teachers. Loving antiquity and withdrawal, I originally sought only the joy of mountains and waters.

sentences.zh: 思率天性以奉至道，豈有意於麋鹿，蓋無心於紱冕。

translations.literal: Thinking to lead my natural disposition in serving the utmost Way—how could there be intent toward elk and deer? It is rather that I have no mind for cord and cap.
translations.idiomatic: I wished to follow my natural disposition in serving the highest Way. How could I have intended to live like elk and deer? I simply had no heart for official rank and emblems of office.

sentences.zh: 其所幸者，邦家化成，疆場兵偃，群黎鼓舞，庶彙胥悅。

translations.literal: What I have been fortunate in is the state's transformation complete, the frontier stilled of arms, the masses drumming with joy, the myriad categories all pleased.
translations.idiomatic: What I have been fortunate to witness is the state's transformation complete, the frontier stilled of arms, the people rejoicing, and all things flourishing in contentment.

sentences.zh: 蒲帛之聘，寵渙巖谷，君命薦及，肅聽祗受。

translations.literal: The summons of rush mat and silk, favor streaming to cliff and valley, the ruler's command reaching down—I reverently heard and respectfully received.
translations.idiomatic: The summons of rush mat and silk brought favor streaming to my cliff and valley. When the ruler's command reached me, I reverently heard and respectfully accepted it.

sentences.zh: 既朝象魏之下，但愧巖林之賤。

translations.literal: Having already attended court beneath the elephant towers, I am only ashamed at the lowliness of cliff and forest.
translations.idiomatic: Having already attended court beneath the imperial towers, I am only ashamed of my lowly station among cliffs and forests.

sentences.zh: 奉聖顏於咫尺，聆德音之教論。

translations.literal: I have attended the sage countenance within arm's reach and heard the virtuous voice's instruction and discourse.
translations.idiomatic: I have been privileged to behold the sage countenance at close hand and to hear the sovereign's instructive discourse.

sentences.zh: 列跡侍從，峨冠諫諍。

translations.literal: I have taken my place among the attendants, high-capped in remonstrance.
translations.idiomatic: I have taken my place among the attendants, wearing the high cap of remonstrance.

sentences.zh: 雖愚者之慮，竭忠規而屢陳；

translations.literal: Though a foolish man's considerations, I have exhausted loyal counsel and repeatedly presented it;
translations.idiomatic: Though only a foolish man's thoughts, I have exhausted loyal counsel and presented it repeatedly;

sentences.zh: 而大君之明，懼瞽言之無補。

translations.literal: yet the great ruler's clarity—I fear a blind man's words are of no help.
translations.idiomatic: yet before the great ruler's clarity I fear that a blind man's words are of no help.

sentences.zh: 今又訪以禮樂之制，詢其刑政之方，且小器微材，欲加大用。

translations.literal: Now you again inquire about the institutions of rites and music and ask the methods of punishments and government—yet a small vessel and slight timber, you wish to employ greatly.
translations.idiomatic: Now you again inquire about the institutions of rites and music and ask the methods of punishments and government—yet you would employ greatly a small vessel and slight timber such as I.

sentences.zh: 蓋念沿革之攸宜，曆三五而既異，弛張之體，豈一二而可述。

translations.literal: Considering that what is fitting in continuity and change has passed through three and five reigns and is already different, the substance of loosening and tightening—how could one or two points suffice to relate it?
translations.idiomatic: Reflecting that what is fitting in continuity and change has differed through the three and five reigns, and that the principles of loosening and tightening cannot be set forth in one or two points—

sentences.zh: 國家謀建皇極，躋納富壽，惟二聖之光宅，總百王之闕漏，豈伊葑菲，敢預論述。

translations.literal: the state plans to establish the supreme pole and ascend to abundance and longevity—only the two sages' dwelling in light, gathering the hundred kings' gaps and leaks—how could such brambles and felwort dare to take part in discourse?
translations.idiomatic: the state plans to establish the supreme pole and ascend to abundance and longevity under the luminous rule of the two sage emperors, gathering up the omissions of a hundred kings—how could such worthless brambles as I dare to take part in such discourse?

sentences.zh: 方今德義宣明，鸞驥戾止，如臣之才，儼爾駢列。

translations.literal: Just now virtue and righteousness are proclaimed and made clear; phoenixes and thoroughbreds arrive and stop—talents like your subject's stand in rows alongside.
translations.idiomatic: At present virtue and righteousness are proclaimed throughout the realm, and the finest talents gather at court. Men of talent such as your subject stand in rows among them.

sentences.zh: 伏望洞知臣之鑒，憐守節之志，俾泛駕無覆壓之害，使為器免溢蕩之咎，寢此過聽，遂其夙心。

translations.literal: I bow and hope you will thoroughly know your subject's discernment, pity the will to keep integrity, let the overloaded carriage suffer no overturning harm, let the vessel avoid the fault of overflowing and spilling, lay aside this excessive hearing, and fulfill his long-standing heart.
translations.idiomatic: I humbly hope you will perceive my limitations, pity my resolve to keep my integrity, spare the overloaded carriage from being overturned, spare the vessel from overflowing, set aside this excessive favor, and fulfill my long-standing wish.

sentences.zh: 況臣首獻納之行，不為無位；

translations.literal: Moreover, your subject's first service in presentation and acceptance is not without position;
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, your subject has already served in presentation and remonstrance and is not without position;

sentences.zh: 預清閑之對，不為疏隔。

translations.literal: participating in clear and leisurely audiences is not estrangement.
translations.idiomatic: and has participated in leisurely audiences with the sovereign and is not kept at a distance.

sentences.zh: 又安敢碌碌而依違，嘿嘿而曠素？

translations.literal: How again would I dare be mediocre and vacillate, silent and neglect plainness?
translations.idiomatic: How then could I dare to be mediocre and vacillate, silent and neglect my plain duty?

sentences.zh: 願且齒於諫署，庶少觀於朝製，斯亦否能有適，名器無假。

translations.literal: I wish only to be counted among the remonstrance office, hoping briefly to observe court institutions—this also is whether negation can have what fits; titles and vessels need no borrowing.
translations.idiomatic: I wish only to remain counted among the remonstrance office, hoping briefly to observe court institutions. Whether this suits or not, titles and honors need not be borrowed.

sentences.zh: 唯茲保全之惠，仰繄仁聖之賜。」

translations.literal: Only this favor of preservation—I look up and depend on the benevolent sage's grant."
translations.idiomatic: Only this favor of preservation do I look up to and depend upon—the grant of the benevolent and sage sovereign."

sentences.zh: 放屢至闕下，俄復還山，人有詒書嘲其出處之跡，且勸以棄位居岩穀，放不答。

translations.literal: Fang repeatedly came to the capital and soon returned to the mountains; people sent letters mocking his tracks of coming forth and withdrawal and also urging him to abandon office and dwell in cliff and valley—Fang did not reply.
translations.idiomatic: Fang repeatedly came to the capital and soon returned to the mountains. People sent letters mocking his comings and goings between court and seclusion and urging him to abandon office and dwell in the cliffs and valleys. Fang did not reply.

sentences.zh: 放終身不娶，尤惡囂雜，故京城賜第為擇僻處。

translations.literal: Fang never married in his whole life and especially hated noise and clamor; therefore when a residence was granted in the capital a secluded place was chosen.
translations.idiomatic: Fang never married throughout his life and especially hated noise and clamor. When a residence was granted him in the capital, a secluded location was deliberately chosen.

sentences.zh: 然祿賜既優，晚節頗飾輿服。

translations.literal: Yet since salary and gifts were generous, in his later years he quite adorned carriage and dress.
translations.idiomatic: Yet because his salary and gifts were generous, in his later years he quite adorned his carriage and dress.

sentences.zh: 於長安廣置良田，歲利甚博，亦有強市者，遂致爭訟，門人族屬依倚恣橫。

translations.literal: In Chang'an he broadly acquired fertile fields; yearly profit was very great; there were also forced purchases, which led to lawsuits; disciples and kinsmen relied on him and acted wantonly.
translations.idiomatic: In Chang'an he acquired extensive fertile fields, and his yearly profits were very great. There were also cases of forced purchase that led to lawsuits. His disciples and kinsmen relied on his power and acted arrogantly.

sentences.zh: 王嗣宗守京兆，放嘗乘醉慢罵之。

translations.literal: Wang Sizong guarded the capital district; Fang once, taking advantage of drunkenness, insulted and reviled him.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Sizong was governor of the capital district. Fang once, while drunk, insulted and reviled him.

sentences.zh: 嗣宗屢遣人責放不法，仍條上其事。

translations.literal: Sizong repeatedly sent men to reproach Fang for unlawful conduct and also itemized and reported the matter upward.
translations.idiomatic: Sizong repeatedly sent men to reproach Fang for unlawful conduct and also submitted a detailed report to the throne.

sentences.zh: 詔工部郎中施護推究，會赦恩而止。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Shi Hu, bureau director in the Ministry of Works, to investigate; it happened that an amnesty intervened and it stopped.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered Shi Hu, bureau director in the Ministry of Works, to investigate, but an amnesty intervened and the matter was dropped.

sentences.zh: 四月，求歸山，又賜宴遣之。

translations.literal: In the fourth month he requested to return to the mountains; he was again granted a banquet and sent off.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month he requested to return to the mountains. The court again granted him a farewell banquet and sent him on his way.

sentences.zh: 所居山林，細民多縱樵采，特詔禁止。

translations.literal: In the mountains and forests where he dwelt, common people often freely cut firewood; a special edict forbade it.
translations.idiomatic: In the mountains and forests where he lived, common people often freely cut firewood. A special edict forbade this practice.

sentences.zh: 放遂表徙居嵩山天封觀側，遣內侍就興唐觀基起第賜之。

translations.literal: Fang thereupon submitted a memorial reporting his move to dwell beside Tianfeng Observatory on Mount Song; the emperor dispatched a palace attendant to build a mansion on the foundation of the Xingtang Observatory and granted it to him.
translations.idiomatic: Fang then memorialized the throne that he had settled beside Tianfeng Guan on Mount Song; the emperor sent a eunuch to erect a residence on the old site of Xingtang Guan and bestowed it upon him.

sentences.zh: 假踰百日，續給其奉。

translations.literal: His leave was extended past a hundred days, and his allowance continued to be supplied.
translations.idiomatic: His leave of absence was prolonged beyond one hundred days, and his official stipend kept flowing.

sentences.zh: 然猶往來終南，按視田畝。

translations.literal: Yet he still went back and forth to Zhongnan, inspecting fields and mu.
translations.idiomatic: Even so, he continued to travel to the Zhongnan Mountains to oversee his farmland.

sentences.zh: 每行必給驛乘，在道或親詬驛吏，規算糧具之直。

translations.literal: Whenever he traveled he was always given post-station mounts; on the road he sometimes personally reviled post clerks and calculated the price of grain and provisions.
translations.idiomatic: Every journey brought him relay horses from the postal service, yet on the road he would sometimes berate the clerks himself and haggle over the cost of grain and supplies.

sentences.zh: 時議浸薄之。

translations.literal: At the time public discussion gradually treated him lightly.
translations.idiomatic: Opinion in the capital slowly turned against him.

sentences.zh: 嘗曲宴令群臣賦詩，杜鎬以素不屬辭，誦《北山移文》以譏之。

translations.literal: Once at an intimate banquet he ordered the assembled ministers to compose poems; Du Hao, who had never been skilled at verse, recited "Beishan Yi Wen" to mock him.
translations.idiomatic: At one private banquet he required all the ministers present to write poems; Du Hao, no poet by habit, read aloud the "Rhapsody on Removing to the Northern Mountains" as a barb aimed at Fang.

sentences.zh: 上嘗語近臣曰：「放為朕言事甚眾，但外廷無知者。」

translations.literal: The emperor once said to close ministers: "Fang has spoken many matters on Our behalf to Us, yet those outside the inner court know nothing of them."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor once told his inner circle, "Fang has reported a great many affairs to me, but the outer court hears nothing of it."

sentences.zh: 因出所上《時議》十三篇，其目曰：《議道》、《議德》、《議刑》、《議器》、《議文武》、《議制度》、《議教化》、《議賞罰》、《議官司》、《議軍政》、《議獄訟》、《議征賦》、《議邪正》。

translations.literal: Thereupon he produced the thirteen pieces Fang had submitted titled "Timely Discussions," their chapters being: "On the Way," "On Virtue," "On Punishments," "On Implements," "On Civil and Military Affairs," "On Institutions," "On Teaching and Transformation," "On Rewards and Punishments," "On Official Posts," "On Military Administration," "On Prison Litigation," "On Levies and Tribute," and "On the Upright and the Deviant."
translations.idiomatic: He then displayed the thirteen memorials Fang had submitted under the title "Timely Policy Opinions," with these section headings: On the Way, On Virtue, On Punishments, On Implements, On Civil and Military Affairs, On Institutions, On Teaching and Transformation, On Rewards and Punishments, On Official Posts, On Military Administration, On Prison Litigation, On Levies and Tribute, and On the Upright and the Deviant.

sentences.zh: 八年十一月乙丑，晨興，忽取前後章疏稿悉焚之，服道士衣，召諸生會飲於次，酒數行而卒。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of the eighth year, on the day yichou, at morning rising he suddenly took all drafts of his former and later memorials and burned them, put on Taoist robes, summoned his students to drink together in the side hall, and after a few rounds of wine he died.
translations.idiomatic: On yichou, the eleventh month of the eighth year, he rose at dawn, burned every draft of his memorials past and present, dressed as a Daoist priest, called his pupils to drink in the side hall, and died after only a few cups.

sentences.zh: 訃聞，上甚嗟悼，親製文遣內侍朱允中致祭。

translations.literal: When the death report arrived, the emperor deeply sighed in grief, personally composed a text, and sent the palace attendant Zhu Yunzhong to offer sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: When word of his death reached the palace, the emperor mourned deeply, wrote the eulogy himself, and dispatched the eunuch Zhu Yunzhong to perform the rites.
