sentences.zh: 歸葬終南，贈工部尚書，錄其侄世雍同學究出身。

translations.literal: He was returned for burial on Zhongnan; posthumously enfeoffed Minister of Works; his nephew Shiyong was entered as a tong jinshi chushen graduate.
translations.idiomatic: His body was buried on the Zhongnan range; he was posthumously made Minister of Works; and his nephew Shiyong was granted jinshi standing by special record.

sentences.zh: 萬適，字縱之，陳州宛丘人，自號遣玄子。

translations.literal: Wan Shi, styled Zongzhi, was a man of Wancheng in Chenzhou; he styled himself the Hermit Who Sends Off Mystery.
translations.idiomatic: Wan Shi, whose courtesy name was Zongzhi, came from Wancheng in Chen Prefecture and called himself the Disperser of the Mysterious.

sentences.zh: 六七歲即為詩。

translations.literal: At six or seven sui he was already composing poetry.
translations.idiomatic: He was writing verse by the age of six or seven.

sentences.zh: 及長，喜學問，精於《道德經》。

translations.literal: When grown, he delighted in learning and was expert in the Daodejing.
translations.idiomatic: As an adult he took joy in scholarship and knew the Daodejing thoroughly.

sentences.zh: 與高錫族子冕及韓伾交遊，酬唱多有警句。

translations.literal: He associated in friendship with Gao Xi's clansman Mian and Han Yi; in exchanged verses many startling lines appeared.
translations.idiomatic: He kept company with Mian, a kinsman of Gao Xi, and Han Yi, and their poetic exchanges often yielded memorable lines.

sentences.zh: 不求仕進，專以著述為務，有《狂簡集》百卷、《雅書》三卷、《誌苑》三卷、《雍熙詩》二百首，《經籍擿科討論》計四十卷。

translations.literal: He did not seek advancement in office, devoting himself solely to authorship; he had "Kuangjian Ji" in a hundred juan, "Yashu" in three juan, "Zhih Yuan" in three juan, two hundred pieces of "Yongxi Shi," and "Jingji Tike Taolun" totaling forty juan.
translations.idiomatic: He refused official career and wrote full-time, leaving works that included the hundred-scroll Kuangjian Collection, three scrolls each of Elegant Writings and the Record Garden, two hundred Yongxi poems, and forty scrolls of textual criticism on the classics.

sentences.zh: 淳化中，伾任翰林學士，因召對，上問曰：「卿早在嵩陽，當時輩流頗有遺逸否？」

translations.literal: In the Chunhua era, Yi served as Hanlin academician; summoned to audience, the emperor asked: "You were early at Songyang—were there many recluses among your contemporaries there?"
translations.idiomatic: During Chunhua, Han Yi became a Hanlin academician; at an imperial audience the emperor asked, "You spent your youth at Songyang—did any notable recluses remain among your circle there?"

sentences.zh: 伾以適及楊璞、田誥為對，上悉令召至闕下。

translations.literal: Yi answered with Shi, Yang Pu, and Tian Hao; the emperor ordered all summoned to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Yi named Wan Shi, Yang Pu, and Tian Hao; the emperor commanded that all three be brought to court.

sentences.zh: 詔書下而誥卒。

translations.literal: When the imperial edict descended, Hao had already died.
translations.idiomatic: The summons arrived the day Tian Hao died.

sentences.zh: 璞既至，對於便殿，不願仕進，上賜以束帛，與一子出身，遣還故郡。

translations.literal: Once Pu arrived he answered in the informal hall, unwilling to seek office; the emperor bestowed silks, granted one son chushen standing, and sent him back to his home commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Pu came to the privy audience hall, declined any post, received bolts of silk and an honorary degree for one son, and was sent home.

sentences.zh: 適最後至，特授慎縣主簿。

translations.literal: Shi arrived last and was specially appointed Chief Clerk of Shen County.
translations.idiomatic: Wan Shi was the last to arrive and was made chief clerk of Shen County by special appointment.

sentences.zh: 適素康強無疾，詔下日已病，猶勉強赴朝謝，舉止山野，人皆笑之，後數日卒。

translations.literal: Shi had always been sturdy and without illness; the day the edict came down he was already ill, yet still forced himself to attend court to give thanks; his deportment was rough and rustic—all laughed—and several days later he died.
translations.idiomatic: Wan Shi had been hale, but the day the summons came he fell ill; he still dragged himself to court to acknowledge the appointment, moved like a country bumpkin amid the courtiers' laughter, and died within days.

sentences.zh: 田誥者，歷城人。

translations.literal: Tian Hao was a man of Licheng.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Hao came from Licheng.

sentences.zh: 好著述，聚學徒數百人，舉進士至顯達者接踵，以故聞名於朝，宋惟翰、許袞皆其弟子也。

translations.literal: He loved authorship, gathered several hundred disciples; those who passed the jinshi examination and reached eminence followed one upon another—for this he became known at court; Song Weihan and Xu Gun were both his pupils.
translations.idiomatic: A prolific author who gathered hundreds of students, he sent a steady stream of disciples to jinshi success and fame at court; Song Weihan and Xu Gun were among his students.

sentences.zh: 誥著作百餘篇傳於世，大率迂闊。

translations.literal: Hao's compositions, more than a hundred pieces transmitted in the world, were for the most part circumlocutory and broad.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Hao left over a hundred works in circulation, most of them diffuse and grandiose.

sentences.zh: 每構思必匿深草中，絕不聞人聲，俄自草中躍出，即一篇成矣。

translations.literal: Whenever he conceived a text he hid deep in tall grass where no human voice was heard; suddenly he would leap out of the grass and one complete piece was finished.
translations.idiomatic: To compose, he would vanish into deep grass where no one could disturb him, then burst out with a finished essay in hand.

sentences.zh: 楊璞字契玄，鄭州新鄭人。

translations.literal: Yang Pu, styled Qixuan, was a man of Xinzheng in Zhengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Pu, courtesy name Qixuan, was from Xinzheng in Zheng Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 善歌詩，士大夫多傳誦。

translations.literal: He was skilled at chanting poetry; scholar-officials widely transmitted and recited his works.
translations.idiomatic: A gifted poet whose verses circulated widely among the gentry.

sentences.zh: 與畢士安尤相善，每乘牛往來郭店，自稱東裏遺民。

translations.literal: He was especially friendly with Bi Shian; they often rode oxen back and forth to Guodian, styling himself a leftover subject of Dongli.
translations.idiomatic: He was especially close to Bi Shian; the two would ride oxen to Guodian, and Pu called himself a leftover man of the eastern lanes.

sentences.zh: 嘗杖策入嵩山窮絕處，構思為歌詩，凡數年得百餘篇。

translations.literal: Once leaning on a staff he entered the most remote reaches of Mount Song to conceive chant-poetry; in several years he obtained more than a hundred pieces.
translations.idiomatic: He once walked with staff into the farthest recesses of Mount Song to compose, gathering more than a hundred poems over several years.

sentences.zh: 璞既被召，還，作《歸耕賦》以見誌。

translations.literal: After Pu was summoned and returned, he composed "Guigeng Fu" to show his resolve.
translations.idiomatic: After his summons and return, Yang Pu wrote the "Rhapsody on Returning to the Plough" to declare his intent.

sentences.zh: 真宗朝諸陵，道出鄭州，遣使以茶帛賜之。

translations.literal: When Zhenzong visited the imperial tombs, his route passed Zhengzhou; he sent envoys to bestow tea and silks on him.
translations.idiomatic: On a tomb visit Zhenzong passed through Zhengzhou and sent gifts of tea and silk.

sentences.zh: 卒，年七十八。

translations.literal: He died at age seventy-eight.
translations.idiomatic: He died at seventy-eight.

sentences.zh: 李瀆，河南洛陽人也。

translations.literal: Li Du was a man of Luoyang in Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Li Du came from Luoyang in Henan.

sentences.zh: 六世祖坦，馮翊令。

translations.literal: His sixth-generation ancestor Tan was magistrate of Fufeng.
translations.idiomatic: Six generations back his forebear Tan had served as magistrate of Fufeng.

sentences.zh: 坦生仲芳，大理司直。

translations.literal: Tan begot Zhongfang, Directing Clerk in the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: Tan's son Zhongfang became a directing clerk in the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 仲芳生玄初，福建觀察推官。

translations.literal: Zhongfang begot Xuanchu, pushing officer under the Fujian Observation Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongfang's son Xuanchu served as a legal aide to the Fujian observation commissioner.

sentences.zh: 玄初生鄑，即瀆之曾祖也，字堯封，仕梁，曆滑、魏、宋三鎮留後，拜崇政使、禮部尚書。

translations.literal: Xuanchu begot Zou, Du's great-grandfather; style name Yaofeng; he served Liang, passed through the three military commissioners of Hua, Wei, and Song, and was appointed Commissioner for Esteeming Governance and Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanchu's son Zou—Li Du's great-grandfather, styled Yaofeng—served the Liang, held successive posts as military commissioner at Hua, Wei, and Song, and rose to commissioner for esteeming governance and minister of rites.

sentences.zh: 後唐天成中，以太子少傅致仕，卒，贈太保。

translations.literal: In Tiancheng of Later Tang he retired as Junior Tutor to the Heir Apparent; on death he was posthumously enfeoffed Grand Tutor.
translations.idiomatic: In the Tiancheng reign of Later Tang he retired as junior tutor to the heir apparent and, after death, was posthumously named grand tutor.

sentences.zh: 祖延昭，殿中丞。

translations.literal: His grandfather Yanzhao was Assistant in the Palace.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Yanzhao was an assistant in the palace directorate.

sentences.zh: 父瑩字正白，善詞賦，廣順進士，蒲帥張鐸辟為記室，因家河中。

translations.literal: His father Ying, style name Zhengbai, was skilled at lyric rhapsody; a Guangshun jinshi; Hedong military commissioner Zhang Duo recruited him as recorder; thus the family settled in the Hezhong region.
translations.idiomatic: His father Ying, styled Zhengbai, excelled at fu verse, passed the jinshi in Guangshun, entered the staff of Zhang Duo, military commissioner of Hedong, and made his home in the Hezhong region.

sentences.zh: 乾德初，右補闕蘇德祥薦為殿中侍御史、度支判官。

translations.literal: Early in Qiande, Remonstrance Censor Su Dexiang recommended him as Palace Attendant Censor and fiscal commissioner judge.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Qiande, remonstrance censor Su Dexiang recommended him for palace attendant censor and fiscal commission judge.

sentences.zh: 使江南，坐受李從善賂遺，責授右讚善大夫，卒。

translations.literal: On mission to Jiangnan, he was convicted of receiving bribes and gifts from Li Congshan; demoted to Right Director of Advising; he died.
translations.idiomatic: On an embassy to the south he accepted bribes from Li Congshan, was reduced to right director of advising, and died.

sentences.zh: 初，瑩禱河祠而生瀆，故名瀆字河神，後改字長源。

translations.literal: At first, when Ying prayed at the River shrine and Du was born, he was therefore named Du with style River God; later the style was changed to Changyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Ying had prayed at a river shrine when Li Du was born, so the boy was first styled River God; he later took the courtesy name Changyuan.

sentences.zh: 淳澹好古，博覽經史。

translations.literal: Simple, tranquil, and fond of antiquity, he broadly read the classics and histories.
translations.idiomatic: Quiet and antiquarian by nature, he read widely in the classics and histories.

sentences.zh: 十六丁外艱，服闕，杜門不復仕進。

translations.literal: At sixteen he underwent mourning for his father; when mourning ended he shut his door and no longer sought office.
translations.idiomatic: He mourned his father from sixteen; when the mourning period ended, he closed his gates and never sought office again.

sentences.zh: 家世多聚書畫，頗有奇妙。

translations.literal: For generations the family gathered books and paintings, with quite a few remarkable pieces.
translations.idiomatic: The family hoarded books and paintings over generations, including many masterpieces.

sentences.zh: 王祐典河中，深加禮待，自是多聞於時。

translations.literal: When Wang You governed Hezhong he deeply honored and treated him; from then he was much heard of in the age.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang You governed Hezhong he treated Li Du with exceptional respect, and fame followed.

sentences.zh: 往來中條山中，不親產業，所居木石幽勝。

translations.literal: He went back and forth in the Zhongtiao Mountains, not personally managing property; where he dwelt, trees and stone were secluded and excellent.
translations.idiomatic: He wandered the Zhongtiao range, ignoring his estates, in retreats where timber and stone composed a perfect solitude.

sentences.zh: 談唐室已來衣冠人物，歷歷可聽。

translations.literal: Speaking of eminent figures since the Tang house, his accounts were clearly sequential and worth hearing.
translations.idiomatic: When he spoke of celebrated men since the Tang, every name fell into place like a living chronicle.

sentences.zh: 罕著文。

translations.literal: He rarely composed written pieces.
translations.idiomatic: He seldom put pen to paper.

sentences.zh: 前後州將皆厚遇之。

translations.literal: Successive provincial commanders all treated him generously.
translations.idiomatic: Every prefect who held the region treated him generously.

sentences.zh: 王旦、李宗諤與之世舊，每勸其仕，瀆皆不答。

translations.literal: Wang Dan and Li Zong'e were hereditary friends with him; each time they urged him to take office, Du made no reply.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dan and Li Zong'e, old family friends, repeatedly urged him into service; Li Du never answered.

sentences.zh: 所乘馬，嘗為宗人借，憩於廛間。

translations.literal: The horse he rode was once borrowed by a clansman and rested in the marketplace quarter.
translations.idiomatic: A clansman once borrowed his horse and left it tethered in a busy market street.

sentences.zh: 人有見者以語瀆，瀆即鬻之，其惡囂如此。

translations.literal: Someone who saw this told Du; Du immediately sold it—such was his hatred of clamor.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Du learned of it, he sold the horse at once—so deep was his loathing of bustle.

sentences.zh: 州閭化其儉德。

translations.literal: Within the prefecture the neighborhoods were transformed by his frugal virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Neighbors across the prefecture took their cue from his austere ways.

sentences.zh: 真宗祀汾陰，直史館孫冕言其隱操，請加搜采，陳堯叟復薦之。

translations.literal: When Zhenzong sacrificed at Fenyin, Direct Historian Sun Mian spoke of his hidden integrity and requested intensified search and collection; Chen Yaosou again recommended him.
translations.idiomatic: During Zhenzong's Fengyin sacrifice, Sun Mian praised his reclusive integrity and urged that he be sought out; Chen Yaosou seconded the recommendation.

sentences.zh: 命使召見，辭足疾不起。

translations.literal: He was ordered summoned for audience; he declined on grounds of foot ailment and did not rise to go.
translations.idiomatic: Envoys were sent to summon him, but he pleaded lameness and refused to come.

sentences.zh: 遣內侍勞問，令長吏歲時存撫。

translations.literal: A palace attendant was sent to console and inquire; the senior prefectural official was ordered to visit and care for him at the seasons of the year.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent a eunuch with greetings and told the prefect to check on him throughout the year.

sentences.zh: 明年，又遣使存問，瀆自陳世本儒墨習靜避世之意。

translations.literal: The next year envoys were again sent to inquire of him; Du himself stated his family's origin in Ru-Mo practice and intent of cultivating quiet and avoiding the world.
translations.idiomatic: The following year another envoy came; Li Du explained that his family had long followed Confucian and Mohist teaching and that he meant to live in stillness away from the world.

sentences.zh: 素嗜酒，人或勉之，答曰：「扶羸養疾，舍此莫可。

translations.literal: He had always been fond of wine; when others urged him to stop, he replied: "Supporting weakness and nourishing illness—apart from this there is nothing.
translations.idiomatic: He had always loved wine; when friends urged restraint, he said, "To nurse a frail body and a lingering ailment, nothing else will do.

sentences.zh: 從吾所好，以盡餘年，不亦樂乎！」

translations.literal: Follow what I love and exhaust the remaining years—is this not also joy!"
translations.idiomatic: To spend what is left of my life doing what I love—what could be happier?"

sentences.zh: 嘗語諸子曰：「山水足以娛情，苟遇醉而卒，吾之願也。

translations.literal: Once he told his sons: "Mountains and waters suffice to please the feelings; if by chance I meet drunkenness and die—that is my wish.
translations.idiomatic: He told his sons, "Mountains and streams are pleasure enough; if I should die drunk, that is my wish.

sentences.zh: 吾將與爾永訣，爾輩當常在左右。」

translations.literal: I am about to take eternal leave of you; you all should always be at my side."
translations.idiomatic: I am saying farewell for good; you must stay by me always."

sentences.zh: 即設外寢，與諸子同處。

translations.literal: Thereupon he set up an outer sleeping chamber and dwelt together with his sons.
translations.idiomatic: He moved his bed to an outer room and would not let his sons leave him.

sentences.zh: 一日，忽曰：「適有人至床下，誦詩云：『行到水窮處，未知天盡時。』

translations.literal: One day he suddenly said: "Just now someone came beneath the bed and recited a poem saying: 'Having walked to where the waters end, one does not yet know when heaven will end.
translations.idiomatic: One day he said abruptly, "Someone just came to my bedside and recited: 'You have walked to where the waters end, yet do not know when heaven itself will end.

sentences.zh: 言訖不見，吾當逝矣。」

translations.literal: When the words ended the figure was not seen; "I am about to depart."
translations.idiomatic: When the voice ceased the visitor vanished. "It is time for me to go," he said."

sentences.zh: 亟取瑩集七十編洎書畫付諸子，促家人置酒。

translations.literal: He hurriedly took Ying's collected works in seventy series together with paintings and calligraphy and handed them to his sons, urging the household to set out wine.
translations.idiomatic: He quickly gave his sons Ying's seventy-scroll collected works and the family's paintings, then told the household to bring wine.

sentences.zh: 頃之，卒。

translations.literal: Shortly after, he died.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was dead.

sentences.zh: 時天禧三十年十二月三日也，年六十三。

translations.literal: At the time it was the third day of the twelfth month in the thirtieth year of Tianxi; he was sixty-three.
translations.idiomatic: It was the third day of the twelfth month in the third year of Tianxi; he was sixty-three.

sentences.zh: 四年春，詔曰：「故河中府處士李瀆，簪纓傳緒，儒雅踐方，曠逸自居，恬智交養。

translations.literal: In spring of the fourth year an edict said: "The late Recluse Li Du of Hezhong Prefecture, with official caps transmitted in lineage, practiced Confucian elegance and rectitude, dwelt in expansive withdrawal, and mutually nourished tranquility and wisdom.
translations.idiomatic: In spring of the fourth year an edict declared: "The late recluse Li Du of Hezhong came from a line of office-holders, lived by Confucian refinement and integrity, chose spacious seclusion, and cultivated both calm and insight.

sentences.zh: 迨茲晚節，彌邵清猷，奄及淪亡，良深軫惻。

translations.literal: Reaching this late season of life, he ever more displayed pure designs; suddenly he met ruin and perishing—truly deep is Our heartfelt grief.
translations.idiomatic: In his later years his conduct grew ever purer; his sudden passing moves Us to deep sorrow.

sentences.zh: 特行賁典，式慰營魂。

translations.literal: We specially confer a splendid rite to comfort the soul dwelling in the grave mound.
translations.idiomatic: We therefore grant a special posthumous honor to comfort his spirit.

sentences.zh: 惟蓬閣之司文，乃儒林之美秩。

translations.literal: Only the director of writing in the Penglai Pavilion is a beautiful rank of the Confucian forest.
translations.idiomatic: The post of literary compiler in the Hanlin archives is among the finest offices of the scholarly world.

sentences.zh: 仍示歸生之賻，兼推給復之恩。

translations.literal: We also display funerary gifts for the returning living and jointly extend the grace of exemption from corvée.
translations.idiomatic: We further bestow burial gifts and extend tax and labor exemptions on his household.

sentences.zh: 申飭守臣，優恤其後。

translations.literal: We instruct the guarding ministers to treat his survivors with generous care.
translations.idiomatic: Local officials are charged to look after his family with special kindness.

sentences.zh: 豈獨旌於泉壤，亦足厚於民風。

translations.literal: How could this honor only the springs and soil? It is also sufficient to enrich popular custom.
translations.idiomatic: This honors him not only beneath the earth but also strengthens the manners of the people.

sentences.zh: 可特贈秘書省著作佐郎，賜其家帛二十匹，米三十斛，州縣常加存恤，二稅外蠲其差役。」

translations.literal: He may be specially posthumously enfeoffed Assistant Compiler in the Secretariat, with twenty bolts of silk and thirty hu of rice granted to his family; prefectures and counties shall regularly add care and relief; apart from the two taxes, his corvée and labor duties are remitted."
translations.idiomatic: Let him be posthumously made Assistant Compiler in the Secretariat; grant his household twenty bolts of silk and thirty hu of grain; prefectural and county officials shall watch over them; and all labor levies beyond the regular taxes are waived."

sentences.zh: 魏野，字仲先，陝州陝人也。

translations.literal: Wei Ye, styled Zhongxian, was a man of Shan in Shanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Ye, whose courtesy name was Zhongxian, came from Shan in Shan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 世為農。

translations.literal: For generations they were farmers.
translations.idiomatic: His family had farmed for generations.

sentences.zh: 母嘗夢引袂於月中承兔得之，因有娠，遂生野。

translations.literal: His mother once dreamed of drawing her sleeve in the moon to receive a rabbit and obtain it; because of this she conceived, and thus Ye was born.
translations.idiomatic: His mother dreamed she reached into the moon with her sleeve to catch a rabbit; she conceived and bore Wei Ye.

sentences.zh: 及長，嗜吟詠，不求聞達。

translations.literal: When grown, he was fond of chanting and singing; he did not seek fame and advancement.
translations.idiomatic: As an adult he loved poetry and sought neither office nor renown.

sentences.zh: 居州之東郊，手植竹樹，清泉環繞，旁對雲山，景趣幽絕。

translations.literal: He dwelt in the eastern suburbs of the prefecture, personally planting bamboo and trees; clear springs encircled it; facing clouded mountains at the side, the scene's interest was secluded to the utmost.
translations.idiomatic: He lived in the eastern suburbs, planting bamboo and trees by hand; clear springs ringed his home and cloud-wrapped peaks rose before him in exquisite seclusion.

sentences.zh: 鑿土袤丈，曰樂天洞，前為草堂，彈琴其中，好事者多載酒肴從之遊，嘯詠終日。

translations.literal: He cut earth one zhang in breadth, calling it Letian Cave; before it he built a thatched hall and played the zither within; many who delighted in such things loaded wine and food to follow him in travel, whistling and chanting all day.
translations.idiomatic: He carved out a one-zhang cave called Letian Dong, set a thatched hall before it, and played the zither there; admirers brought wine and food to join him, and they would chant and whistle away the day.

sentences.zh: 前後郡守，雖武臣舊相，皆所禮遇，或親造謁。

translations.literal: Successive prefects, though military ministers or former chancellors, all honored and treated him, some personally coming to call.
translations.idiomatic: Prefects who followed—whether generals or former chief ministers—all treated him with respect, and some called on him in person.

sentences.zh: 趙昌言性尤倨傲，特署賓次，戒閽吏野至即報。

translations.literal: Zhao Changyan's nature was especially proud and arrogant; he specially assigned a guest seat and warned the gate clerk: when Ye arrives, report at once.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Changyan, notoriously proud, reserved a seat of honor for him and ordered the gatekeeper to announce him the moment he arrived.

sentences.zh: 野不喜巾幘，無貴賤，皆紗帽白衣以見，出則跨白驢。

translations.literal: Ye did not like turban and cap; without regard to noble or base, all met him in gauze cap and white robes; going out he straddled a white donkey.
translations.idiomatic: He disdained formal headgear and received everyone alike in gauze cap and white robes; abroad he rode a white donkey.

sentences.zh: 過客居士往來留題會話，累宿而去。

translations.literal: Traveling guests and retired scholars came and went, leaving inscriptions and conversing, staying several nights before departing.
translations.idiomatic: Travelers and fellow recluses came and went, leaving poems on his walls and talking late into the night for days at a time.

sentences.zh: 野為詩精苦，有唐人風格，多警策句。

translations.literal: Ye's poetry was refined and arduous; it had Tang-person style, with many startling and admonitory lines.
translations.idiomatic: His poetry was painstakingly crafted in the Tang manner, full of striking lines.

sentences.zh: 所有《草堂集》十卷，大中祥符初契丹使至，嘗言本國得其上帙，願求全部，詔與之。

translations.literal: He possessed "Caotang Ji" in ten juan; early in Dazhong Xiangfu when a Khitan envoy arrived, he once said his state had obtained the first fascicle and wished to seek the complete work; an edict granted it.
translations.idiomatic: He left a ten-scroll Caotang Collection; early in Dazhong Xiangfu a Liao envoy said his court had acquired the first fascicle and asked for the complete set, and the emperor ordered it sent.

sentences.zh: 祀汾陰歲，與李瀆並被薦，遣陝令王希招之，野上言曰：「陛下告成天地，延聘岩藪，臣實愚戇，資性慵拙，幸逢聖世，獲安故里，早樂吟詠，實匪風騷，豈意天慈，曲垂搜引。

translations.literal: In the year of the Fengyin sacrifice, together with Li Du he was recommended; the Shan magistrate Wang Xi was sent to summon him; Ye submitted saying: "Your Majesty has announced completion to Heaven and Earth and extended invitation to cliff and thicket; your subject is truly stupid and blunt, his nature lazy and clumsy; fortunately meeting the sage age, he obtains peace in his old home; long delighting in chant and song, truly not of the Feng-Sao tradition—how could he expect Heaven's kindness to bend low in search and drawing forth?
translations.idiomatic: The year of the Fengyin rites he was recommended along with Li Du; Magistrate Wang Xi of Shan was sent to summon him. Wei Ye memorialized: "Your Majesty has reported success to Heaven and Earth and now seeks recluses in the hills. I am dull by nature and indolent by habit. In this enlightened age I live quietly at home and take joy only in verse—not in the grand tradition of the poets. I never dreamed Your Majesty would single me out.

sentences.zh: 但以嘗嬰心疾，尤疏禮節，麋鹿之性，頓纓則狂，豈可瞻對殿墀，仰奉清燕。

translations.literal: Only because he has once suffered heart ailment, especially neglectful of ritual and decorum, with the nature of elk and deer—if the bridle is suddenly set, he goes mad; how could he gaze face to face on the palace steps and look up to receive clear leisure?
translations.idiomatic: I have long suffered from heart trouble and am unfit for court etiquette. I am like a deer—put a halter on me and I bolt wild. How could I stand before the throne or attend Your Majesty's refined company?

sentences.zh: 望回過聽，許令愚守，則畎畝之間，永荷帝力。」

translations.literal: He hopes Your Majesty will turn back excessive hearing and permit him stupid guarding; then between furrow and field he will forever bear the emperor's strength."
translations.idiomatic: I beg you to reconsider and let me remain in my folly at home; then in my fields I shall forever owe your grace."

sentences.zh: 詔州縣長吏常加存撫，又遣使圖其所居觀之。

translations.literal: An edict ordered prefectural and county senior officials regularly to add care and comfort; envoys were also sent to paint his dwelling for viewing.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered local officials to look after him and sent artists to paint his retreat for the court.

sentences.zh: 五年四月，復遣內侍存問。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the fifth year, a palace attendant was again sent to inquire of him.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the fifth year another eunuch was sent with imperial greetings.

sentences.zh: 天禧三年十二月，無疾而卒，年六十。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of the third year of Tianxi, without illness he died, aged sixty.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of the third year of Tianxi he died suddenly, at sixty.

sentences.zh: 州上其狀。

translations.literal: The prefecture reported his circumstances upward.
translations.idiomatic: The prefecture reported his death to the court.

sentences.zh: 四年正月，詔曰：「國家舉旌賞之命，以輝丘園，申恤贈之恩，用慰泉壤，所以褒逸民而厚風俗也。

translations.literal: In the first month of the fourth year an edict said: "The state raises commands of banner and reward to make hill and garden shine; extends the grace of condolence and posthumous gift to comfort springs and soil—thereby to praise withdrawn subjects and enrich popular custom.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the fourth year an edict declared: "The state honors recluses to brighten the hills and gardens, and extends posthumous kindness to comfort the dead—thus to praise men who withdraw from the world and to strengthen public morals.

sentences.zh: 故陝州處士魏野，服膺儒素，刻意篇章，顧詞格之清新，為士流之推許，而能篤淳古之行，慕肥遁之風。

translations.literal: The late Recluse Wei Ye of Shanzhou, embracing Confucian plainness in the breast, carved his intent in chapters and sections; considering his diction and pattern fresh and clear, he was pushed and approved by the scholar stream; yet able to be sincere in pure antiquity's conduct, he admired the wind of fat withdrawal.
translations.idiomatic: The late recluse Wei Ye of Shan Prefecture lived by Confucian simplicity and devoted himself to verse; his fresh style won praise among scholars, and he steadfastly practiced the ways of antiquity, cherishing the ideal of deep withdrawal from the world.

sentences.zh: 頃屬時巡，嘗加聘召，懇陳誠誌，願遂《考槃》。

translations.literal: Recently belonging to the imperial progress of the age, he was once added to summons and invitation; earnestly he stated his sincere resolve, wishing to fulfill "Kaopan."
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor toured the realm he was summoned, but earnestly declared his wish to live out the recluse's life celebrated in the "Kaopan" ode.

sentences.zh: 及此淪亡，載深嗟悼！

translations.literal: When he has now passed away, [We] bear deep lamentation and mourning!
translations.idiomatic: Now that he is gone, our grief runs very deep!

sentences.zh: 蘭台清秩，追飾幽扃，厚其賻助之資，寬以復除之命。

translations.literal: Let the pure rank of the Orchid Terrace be granted posthumously, embellish the dark door [of the tomb], enrich the resources of funeral gifts and aid, and grant lenience with orders of exemption from labor and levies.
translations.idiomatic: We grant him the pure office of the Secretariat archives, adorn his tomb, increase the gifts bestowed on his household, and confer generous exemptions from corvée and other levies.

sentences.zh: 諒惟優禮，式顯令名。

translations.literal: Surely it is only superior courtesy, thereby displaying his excellent name.
translations.idiomatic: Such is the honor we mean to show him, that his fine reputation may shine forth.

sentences.zh: 魂而有知，歆此殊渥。

translations.literal: If the soul has consciousness, savor this extraordinary favor.
translations.idiomatic: If his spirit is aware, let it receive this extraordinary grace.

sentences.zh: 可特贈秘書省著作郎，賻其家帛二十匹，米三十斛，州縣常加存恤，二稅外免其差徭。」

translations.literal: He may be specially posthumously granted Authoring Gentleman of the Secretariat, given to his family twenty bolts of silk and thirty hu of rice; the prefecture and county shall regularly extend care and support; beyond the two taxes, his corvée and levies are exempted."
translations.idiomatic: He is to receive the posthumous title of Authoring Gentleman in the Secretariat; his family shall receive twenty bolts of silk and thirty hu of rice. The local officials shall look after them on a regular basis, and beyond the regular land taxes they shall be freed from corvée and other duties."

sentences.zh: 瀆即野中表兄也。

translations.literal: Du was Ye's cousin on his mother's side.
translations.idiomatic: Li Du was Wei Ye's maternal cousin.

sentences.zh: 瀆卒訃至，野哭之慟，謂其子曰：「吾不可去，去必不至。」

translations.literal: When word of Du's death arrived, Ye wept for him with intense grief and said to his son: "I cannot go; if I go I will surely not arrive."
translations.idiomatic: When news of Li Du's death arrived, Wei Ye mourned him bitterly and told his son, "I cannot go myself—if I go, I will never get there."

sentences.zh: 第遣其子赴之，裁六日而野亦卒，時甚異焉。

translations.literal: He only sent his son to attend; barely six days later Ye also died—at the time this was regarded as very strange.
translations.idiomatic: He sent only his son to the funeral. Six days later Wei Ye himself died as well, and people at the time regarded it as extraordinary.

sentences.zh: 林逋，字君復，杭州錢塘人。

translations.literal: Lin Bu, styled Junfu, was a man of Qiantang in Hangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Lin Bu, whose courtesy name was Junfu, came from Qiantang in Hang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 少孤，力學，不為章句。

translations.literal: Orphaned young, he studied diligently and did not pursue philological commentary.
translations.idiomatic: He lost his parents early and threw himself into learning, but cared little for textual annotation.

sentences.zh: 性恬淡好古，弗趨榮利，家貧衣食不足，晏如也。

translations.literal: By nature calm and fond of antiquity, he did not rush after glory and profit; though his family was poor and lacked sufficient food and clothing, he was entirely at ease.
translations.idiomatic: Quiet by temperament and devoted to the past, he shunned rank and gain; though his household was poor and often short of food and clothing, he remained entirely content.

sentences.zh: 初放遊江、淮間，久之歸杭州，結廬西湖之孤山，二十年足不及城市。

translations.literal: At first he roamed freely between the Yangtze and Huai regions; after long time he returned to Hangzhou, built a hut on Solitary Hill of West Lake, and for twenty years his feet did not reach the city.
translations.idiomatic: He first wandered freely along the Yangtze and Huai, then returned to Hangzhou and built a cottage on Solitary Hill beside West Lake; for twenty years he never set foot in the city.

sentences.zh: 真宗聞其名，賜粟帛，詔長吏歲時勞問。

translations.literal: Emperor Zhenzong heard his name, bestowed grain and silks, and ordered the chief officials to visit and inquire annually at the season.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Zhenzong heard of him, he sent grain and silk and ordered the local magistrates to call on him with gifts each year.

sentences.zh: 薛映、李及在杭州，每造其廬，清談終日而去。

translations.literal: Xue Ying and Li Ji, when in Hangzhou, each visited his hut, conversed at leisure all day, and then departed.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Xue Ying and Li Ji were stationed at Hangzhou, they would visit his cottage, talk with him through the day, and then leave.

sentences.zh: 嘗自為墓於其廬側。

translations.literal: He once built his own tomb beside his hut.
translations.idiomatic: He even prepared his own grave beside his dwelling.

sentences.zh: 臨終為詩，有「茂陵他日求遺稿，猶喜曾無《封禪書》」之句。

translations.literal: On his deathbed he composed a poem with the line, "At Maoling one day they will seek his drafts, yet rejoice that there was never a Book of the Feng and Shan Sacrifices."
translations.idiomatic: Near death he wrote a poem containing the lines, "One day at Maoling they will hunt for his papers—yet be glad he never left behind a Book of the Feng and Shan Sacrifices."

sentences.zh: 既卒，州為上聞，仁宗嗟悼，賜諡和靖先生，賻粟帛。

translations.literal: After he died, the prefecture reported upward; Emperor Renzong sighed and mourned, bestowed the posthumous title Master Hejing, and gave funeral gifts of grain and silk.
translations.idiomatic: After his death the prefecture reported it to court; Emperor Renzong mourned him, granted him the posthumous title Master Hejing, and sent grain and silk to his household.

sentences.zh: 逋善行書，喜為詩，其詞澄浹峭特，多奇句。

translations.literal: Bu was skilled at running script, delighted in composing poetry; his wording was clear, limpid, steep, and special, with many strange lines.
translations.idiomatic: Lin Bu wrote fine running script and loved poetry; his lines were lucid, spare, and striking, and many of them are singularly memorable.

sentences.zh: 既就稿，隨輒棄之。

translations.literal: Once the draft was complete, he would immediately discard it.
translations.idiomatic: As soon as he finished a poem, he would throw the draft away.

sentences.zh: 或謂：「何不錄以示後世？」

translations.literal: Someone said: "Why not record them to show posterity?"
translations.idiomatic: Someone asked him, "Why not preserve them for later generations?"

sentences.zh: 逋曰：「吾方晦跡林壑，且不欲以詩名一時，況後世乎！」

translations.literal: Bu said: "I am now hiding my traces in forests and ravines, and do not wish to be known by poetry for a time—how much less posterity!"
translations.idiomatic: Lin Bu replied, "I mean to vanish into the hills and woods and have no wish even to be famous for poetry in my own day—let alone in later ages!"

sentences.zh: 然好事者往往竊記之，今所傳尚三百餘篇。

translations.literal: Yet enthusiasts often secretly recorded them; those transmitted today still number more than three hundred pieces.
translations.idiomatic: Admirers nonetheless copied many of them in secret; more than three hundred of his poems survive today.

sentences.zh: 逋嘗客臨江，時李諮方舉進士，未有知者，逋謂人曰：「此公輔器也。」

translations.literal: Bu once sojourned at Linjiang; at that time Li Zi was taking the jinshi examination and was not yet known; Bu told people: "This man is vessel for chief minister."
translations.idiomatic: While staying in Linjiang, Lin Bu saw Li Zi, then an unknown candidate for the jinshi degree, and remarked to others, "This man is destined for the highest office."

sentences.zh: 及逋卒，諮適罷三司使為州守，為素服，與其門人臨七日，葬之，刻遺句內壙中。

translations.literal: When Bu died, Zi had just left the post of Commissioner of the Three Departments to become a prefectural governor; he wore plain mourning garb, together with his disciples observed the seven-day vigil, buried him, and carved a surviving line inside the burial chamber.
translations.idiomatic: After Lin Bu's death, Li Zi had just stepped down as commissioner of the Three Departments to become a prefect; he put on mourning dress, kept vigil with his disciples for seven days, buried him, and had a line from one of his poems carved inside the tomb.

sentences.zh: 逋不娶，無子，教兄子宥，登進士甲科。

translations.literal: Bu did not marry and had no son; he taught his elder brother's son You, who passed the jinshi in the top tier.
translations.idiomatic: Lin Bu never married and had no children; he raised his nephew You, who passed the jinshi examination in the highest class.

sentences.zh: 宥子大年，頗介潔自喜，英宗時，為侍御史，連被台移出治獄，拒不肯行，為中丞唐介所奏，降知蘄州，卒於官。

translations.literal: You had a son Danian, rather fastidious and pleased with himself; in the time of Emperor Yingzong he served as Attending Censor, was repeatedly transferred by the censorate bureau to go out and handle prison cases, refused and would not go, was memorialized by Vice Censor-in-Chief Tang Jie, was demoted to know Qizhou, and died in office.
translations.idiomatic: You's son Danian was proud and punctilious; under Emperor Yingzong he served as an attending censor, and when the censorate repeatedly ordered him out to supervise prisons he refused to go. Vice censor-in-chief Tang Jie impeached him, he was demoted to prefect of Qizhou, and he died in that post.

sentences.zh: 高懌，字文悅，荊南高季興四世孫。

translations.literal: Gao Yi, styled Wenyue, was fourth-generation descendant of Gao Jixing of Jingnan.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Yi, whose courtesy name was Wenyue, was a fourth-generation descendant of Gao Jixing of Jingnan.

sentences.zh: 幼孤，養於外家。

translations.literal: Orphaned young, he was raised in his mother's family.
translations.idiomatic: He lost his parents in childhood and was brought up by his mother's kin.

sentences.zh: 十三歲能屬文，通經史百家之書。

translations.literal: At thirteen he could compose literary pieces and was versed in the classics, histories, and works of the hundred schools.
translations.idiomatic: At thirteen he could already write essays and had mastered the classics, histories, and the writings of the philosophers.

sentences.zh: 聞种放隱終南山，乃築室豹林穀，從放受業。

translations.literal: Hearing that Zhong Fang dwelt in reclusion on Zhongnan Mountain, he built a dwelling in Leopard Forest Valley and studied under Fang.
translations.idiomatic: Learning that Zhong Fang lived as a recluse on Zhongnan Mountain, he built a house in Leopard Forest Valley and became his student.

sentences.zh: 放奇之，不敢處以弟子行。

translations.literal: Fang regarded him as extraordinary and did not dare treat him with the deportment of teacher to disciple.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong Fang thought him remarkable and would not treat him merely as a pupil.

sentences.zh: 與同時張蕘、許勃號「南山三友」。

translations.literal: Together with his contemporaries Zhang Rao and Xu Bo he was styled "the Three Friends of South Mountain."
translations.idiomatic: He and his contemporaries Zhang Rao and Xu Bo were known as "the Three Friends of the Southern Mountains."

sentences.zh: 會詔舉沈淪草澤，知長安寇準聞其名薦之，辭不起。

translations.literal: It happened that an edict summoned those sunken in obscurity in the grasslands and marshes; Kou Zhun, magistrate of Chang'an, heard his name and recommended him, but he declined and did not rise.
translations.idiomatic: When an edict called for men of talent hidden in obscurity, Kou Zhun, prefect of Chang'an, recommended him on hearing his reputation, but he refused to accept office.

sentences.zh: 景祐中，錄國初侯王後，懌推其弟忻得官。

translations.literal: In the Jingyou era, when descendants of feudal lords and kings of the founding of the state were registered, Yi urged that his younger brother Xin receive an office.
translations.idiomatic: During the Jingyou reign, when the court enrolled descendants of the founding nobility, Gao Yi yielded the appointment to his younger brother Xin.

sentences.zh: 及範雍建京兆府學，召懌講授諸生，席間常數十百人。

translations.literal: When Fan Yong established the metropolitan prefectural school, he summoned Yi to lecture the students; his hall often held several tens or hundreds.
translations.idiomatic: When Fan Yong founded the metropolitan school, Gao Yi was invited to teach; his lectures regularly drew dozens or even hundreds of students.

sentences.zh: 杜衍嘗請賜處士號，乃命為大理評事，懌固辭。

translations.literal: Du Yan once requested that a Recluse title be granted; he was then appointed Assessor of the Court of Judicial Review, but Yi firmly declined.
translations.idiomatic: Du Yan once asked that he be given the title of recluse; the court then appointed him as an assessor in the Court of Judicial Review, but Gao Yi firmly refused.

sentences.zh: 仁宗嘉其守，號安素處士。

translations.literal: Emperor Renzong praised his constancy and titled him Recluse Ansu.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Renzong admired his steadfastness and granted him the title Recluse of Tranquil Simplicity.

sentences.zh: 詔州縣歲時禮遇之，給良田五百畝。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the prefecture and county to honor him with courtesy at the seasons, and granted five hundred mu of good fields.
translations.idiomatic: The throne ordered local officials to honor him with seasonal visits and granted him five hundred mu of fertile land.

sentences.zh: 文彥博表其經術該通，有高世之行，可以勵風俗，詔賜第一區。

translations.literal: Wen Yanbo memorialized that his classical learning was comprehensive, that he had conduct transcending the age that could encourage custom, and an edict bestowed one residential compound of the first rank.
translations.idiomatic: Wen Yanbo reported that his mastery of the classics was thorough and his conduct exemplary enough to inspire society; the court then granted him a fine residence.

sentences.zh: 嘉祐中，就除光祿寺丞，復固辭。

translations.literal: In the Jiayou era he was directly appointed Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments, but again firmly declined.
translations.idiomatic: During the Jiayou reign he was offered the post of vice director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, but once more refused firmly.

sentences.zh: 夢道士持素書聘為白鹿洞主，卒。

translations.literal: He dreamed a Daoist priest held a plain book inviting him to be master of White Deer Grotto, and died.
translations.idiomatic: He dreamed that a Daoist came with a plain scroll inviting him to become master of White Deer Grotto, and then he died.

sentences.zh: 有韓退者，稷山人。

translations.literal: There was Han Tui, a man of Jishan.
translations.idiomatic: There was also Han Tui of Jishan.

sentences.zh: 亦師事种放。

translations.literal: He too studied under Zhong Fang.
translations.idiomatic: He too studied with Zhong Fang.

sentences.zh: 母死，負土成墳，徒跣終喪，去隱嵩山。

translations.literal: When his mother died, he carried earth to form the mound, went barefoot through the mourning period, left and dwelt in reclusion on Mount Song.
translations.idiomatic: After his mother's death he built her tomb with his own hands, went barefoot for the full mourning period, then withdrew to live as a recluse on Mount Song.

sentences.zh: 吳遵路，石延年論其高節。

translations.literal: Wu Zunlu and Shi Yannian praised his lofty integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Zunlu and Shi Yannian spoke of his exemplary integrity.

sentences.zh: 詔賜粟帛，號安逸處士，以壽終。

translations.literal: An edict bestowed grain and silk, titled him Recluse Anyi, and he ended his life in longevity.
translations.idiomatic: The court sent him grain and silk, granted him the title Recluse of Comfortable Ease, and he died at an advanced age.

sentences.zh: 徐復，字復之，建州人。

translations.literal: Xu Fu, styled Fuzhi, was a man of Jianzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Fu, whose courtesy name was Fuzhi, came from Jian Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 初遊京師，舉進士不中。

translations.literal: At first he traveled to the capital, took the jinshi examination and did not pass.
translations.idiomatic: He first went to the capital, where he failed the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 退而學《易》，通流衍卦氣法，自筮知無祿，遂亡進取意。

translations.literal: He withdrew and studied the Changes, mastered the flowing and spreading hexagram qi method, divined for himself and knew he had no emolument, and thus lost all intent to advance.
translations.idiomatic: He then turned to the Book of Changes, mastered methods of hexagram qi circulation, and when divination showed he was fated to hold no office he abandoned all ambition for advancement.

sentences.zh: 遊學淮、浙間數年，益通陰陽、天文、地理、遁甲、占射諸家之說。

translations.literal: He studied while traveling between Huai and Zhe for several years, and further mastered the doctrines of yin and yang, astronomy, geography, dunjia, divination by shooting, and various schools.
translations.idiomatic: After years of study in the Huai and Zhe regions he also mastered yin-yang theory, astronomy, geography, dunjia prognostication, and related arts of divination.

sentences.zh: 他日聽其鄉人林鴻範說《詩》，且言《詩》之所以用於樂者，忽若有得。

translations.literal: One day he heard his fellow townsman Lin Hongfan expound the Odes, who also spoke of how the Odes are applied in music, and suddenly seemed to gain understanding.
translations.idiomatic: One day he heard his townsman Lin Hongfan lecture on the Odes, especially on how poetry serves music, and something suddenly clicked.

sentences.zh: 因以聲器求之，遂悟大樂，於七音、十二律清濁次序及鍾磬侈弇、匏竹高下制度皆洞達。

translations.literal: Thereupon he sought it through sounding instruments, and so comprehended great music; in the order of clear and muddy among the seven tones and twelve pitch pipes, and in the systems of bell and stone broadness and narrowness, gourd and bamboo high and low, he was thoroughly penetrating.
translations.idiomatic: Pursuing music through actual instruments, he grasped the principles of ceremonial music, including the sequence of the seven tones and twelve pitches, and the construction of bells, stones, reeds, and flutes.

sentences.zh: 方仁宗留意於樂，詔天下求知樂者，大臣薦胡瑗，瑗作鍾磬，大變古法。

translations.literal: Just as Emperor Renzong was attentive to music, an edict sought throughout the realm those who knew music; great ministers recommended Hu Yuan, and Yuan made bells and stones, greatly changing ancient methods.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Renzong turned his attention to music, the court sought experts nationwide; Hu Yuan was recommended and redesigned the bells and chimes, departing sharply from ancient practice.

sentences.zh: 復笑曰：「聖人寓器以聲，今不先求其聲而更其器，其可用乎！」

translations.literal: Fu laughed and said: "The sage lodged sound in instruments; now they do not first seek the sound but change the instruments—can these be used!"
translations.idiomatic: Xu Fu laughed and said, "The sages entrusted sound to instruments—yet now you change the instruments before you have found the right sound. How can that work?"

sentences.zh: 後瑗製作皆不效。

translations.literal: Later Yuan's productions all proved ineffective.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Yuan's instruments afterward failed to produce the desired results.

sentences.zh: 范仲淹過潤州，見復問曰：「今以衍卦占之，四夷無變異乎？」

translations.literal: Fan Zhongyan passed through Runzhou, saw Fu and asked: "Now divining by the spreading hexagram method, will the four barbarians show no irregularities?"
translations.idiomatic: When Fan Zhongyan passed through Run Prefecture, he asked Xu Fu, "If we divine by the spreading-hexagram method, will the frontier peoples remain quiet?"

sentences.zh: 復剋西方當用兵，推其月日，後無少差。

translations.literal: Fu determined the west would see military action, calculated the month and day, and afterward there was not the slightest discrepancy.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Fu predicted war in the west, gave the month and day, and events later matched his forecast exactly.

sentences.zh: 慶曆初，與布衣郭京俱召見，帝問天時人事，復對曰：「以京房《易》卦推之，今年所配年月日時，當小過也。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Qingli, together with commoner Guo Jing he was summoned to audience; the emperor asked about seasonal timing and human affairs, and Fu replied: "Pushing by the Changes hexagrams of Jing Fang, the year, month, day, and hour matched this year correspond to Little Excess.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Qingli era he and Guo Jing, a man of the people, were summoned to court. Asked about heaven and human affairs, Xu Fu answered, "By Jing Fang's method of Change hexagrams, the year, month, day, and hour now in force correspond to the hexagram Little Excess.

sentences.zh: 剛失位而不中，其在強君德乎？」

translations.literal: The firm loses position and is not centered—is it perhaps in strengthening the ruler's virtue?"
translations.idiomatic: The strong line is out of place and not centered—does this not call for strengthening the ruler's virtue?"

sentences.zh: 帝又問：「明年主何卦？」

translations.literal: The emperor again asked: "Next year which hexagram will preside?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked further, "Which hexagram will govern next year?"

sentences.zh: 復曰：「《乾》卦用事。」

translations.literal: Fu said: "The Qian hexagram will be in authority."
translations.idiomatic: Xu Fu replied, "The hexagram Qian will be in force."

sentences.zh: 說至九五盡而止。

translations.literal: He explained up to the fifth nine line and stopped.
translations.idiomatic: He explained the hexagram only as far as the fifth line and then stopped.

sentences.zh: 帝又問：「前年京師黑風，何所應？」

translations.literal: The emperor again asked: "The black wind in the capital the year before last—what did it correspond to?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor also asked, "What did the black wind over the capital two years ago portend?"

sentences.zh: 復曰：「其兆在內，豫王喪其應也。」

translations.literal: Fu said: "Its omen was within; the death of Prince of Yu was its correspondence."
translations.idiomatic: Xu Fu said, "The sign lay within the realm—the death of the Prince of Yu was its fulfillment."

sentences.zh: 明日，命為大理評事，固以疾辭，乃賜號衝晦處士，補其子發試秘書省校書郎。

translations.literal: The next day he was appointed Assessor of the Court of Judicial Review, firmly declined on grounds of illness, whereupon he was granted the title Recluse Chonghui, and his son Fa was given probationary appointment as Collator of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: The next day he was named an assessor in the Court of Judicial Review but declined on grounds of illness; the court then granted him the title Recluse of Hidden Brilliance and appointed his son Fa as a collator in the Secretariat on probation.

sentences.zh: 復性高潔，而處世未嘗自異，後居杭州十數年卒。

translations.literal: Fu's nature was lofty and pure, yet in dealing with the world he never made himself different; afterward he dwelt at Hangzhou for more than ten years and died.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Fu was upright and aloof by nature, yet he never put on airs in daily life; he later lived at Hangzhou for more than ten years and died there.

sentences.zh: 郭京者，少任俠，不事家產，平居好言兵。

translations.literal: Guo Jing, in youth chivalrous and bold, did not attend to family property; in ordinary times he delighted in speaking of warfare.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Jing had been a young man of spirit who cared little for family wealth and loved to talk of military affairs.

sentences.zh: 范仲淹、滕宗諒數薦之。

translations.literal: Fan Zhongyan and Teng Zongliang repeatedly recommended him.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Zhongyan and Teng Zongliang recommended him several times.

sentences.zh: 孔文，字寧極，孔子四十六代孫。

translations.literal: Kong Wen, styled Ningji, was forty-sixth-generation descendant of Confucius.
translations.idiomatic: Kong Wen, whose courtesy name was Ningji, was a forty-sixth-generation descendant of Confucius.

sentences.zh: 隱居汝州龍興縣龍山之滍陽城。

translations.literal: He dwelt in reclusion at Zhiyang Fort in Longshan, Longxing County, Ruzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He lived in seclusion at Zhiyang Fort on Long Mountain in Longxing County, Ruzhou.

sentences.zh: 性孤潔，喜讀書。

translations.literal: By nature solitary and pure, he delighted in reading.
translations.idiomatic: Solitary and fastidious by temperament, he loved books.

sentences.zh: 有田數百畝，賦稅常為鄉里先。

translations.literal: He had several hundred mu of fields; his taxes were always first in the village.
translations.idiomatic: He owned several hundred mu of land and was always the first in his district to pay taxes.

sentences.zh: 遇歲饑，分所餘賙不足者，未嘗計有無。

translations.literal: When he encountered famine years, he divided what remained to relieve those insufficient, never calculating whether he had enough or not.
translations.idiomatic: In famine years he gave away what surplus he had to neighbors in need, without counting the cost.

sentences.zh: 聞人之善若出於己，動止必依禮法。

translations.literal: Hearing others' goodness as if it issued from himself, his movements and stops always followed ritual and law.
translations.idiomatic: He rejoiced in others' virtues as though they were his own, and in all conduct he observed ritual propriety.

sentences.zh: 環所居百餘里，人皆愛慕之，見文於路，輒斂衽以避。

translations.literal: For more than a hundred li around where he dwelt, people all admired him; seeing Wen on the road, they would draw their lapels and yield.
translations.idiomatic: For more than a hundred li around his home people loved and respected him; when they met Kong Wen on the road they would straighten their robes and step aside.

sentences.zh: 葬其父，廬墓三年，臥破棺中，日食米一溢。

translations.literal: Burying his father, he built a hut by the tomb for three years, lay in a broken coffin, daily eating one yi of rice.
translations.idiomatic: After burying his father he mourned at the grave for three years, sleeping in a rough coffin and taking only one small measure of rice a day.

sentences.zh: 壁間生紫芝數十本。

translations.literal: On the wall grew several tens of purple fungi.
translations.idiomatic: Dozens of purple lingzhi mushrooms sprouted on the wall of his hut.

sentences.zh: 州以行義聞，賜粟帛，又給復其家。

translations.literal: The prefecture reported his righteous conduct, bestowed grain and silk, and also granted exemption for his household.
translations.idiomatic: The prefecture reported his exemplary conduct; the court sent grain and silk and exempted his household from levies.

sentences.zh: 近臣列薦，授秘書省校書郎致仕。

translations.literal: Nearby ministers arrayed recommendations; he was appointed Collator of the Secretariat with leave to retire.
translations.idiomatic: Court officials recommended him repeatedly, and he was made a collator in the Secretariat with permission to retire.

sentences.zh: 居數年，召為國子監直講，辭不赴，即遷光祿寺丞。

translations.literal: After dwelling several years, he was summoned as Direct Lecturer of the Directorate of Education, declined and did not go, and was immediately promoted to Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments.
translations.idiomatic: Some years later he was summoned as a lecturer in the Directorate of Education, declined to go, and was promptly promoted to vice director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 頃之，起知龍興縣，復辭。

translations.literal: Before long he was raised to know Longxing County, but again declined.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was appointed magistrate of Longxing County, but again refused.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈太常丞。

translations.literal: He died; posthumously gifted Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously granted the rank of vice director of the Court of Imperial Rites.

sentences.zh: 盜嘗入文家，發其廩粟，文避之，縱其所取。

translations.literal: Thieves once entered Wen's home, opened his granary grain; Wen avoided them and let them take what they would.
translations.idiomatic: Robbers once broke into his house and opened his granary; Kong Wen stayed out of their way and let them take what they wanted.

sentences.zh: 嘗逢羸弱者為盜掠奪其貲，文追盜與語，責之以義，解金畀之，使歸所掠。

translations.literal: He once encountered a weak person whose goods a robber had seized; Wen pursued the robber and spoke with him, admonished him with righteousness, untied gold and gave it to him, making him return what was seized.
translations.idiomatic: Once he came upon a frail man whom bandits had robbed; Kong Wen pursued the robbers, reasoned with them on duty and right, gave them money from his own purse, and made them restore what they had taken.

sentences.zh: 居山未嘗逢毒蛇虎豹，或謂之曰：「子毋夜行，此亦可畏。」

translations.literal: Dwelling in the mountains he never encountered venomous snakes, tigers, or leopards; someone said to him: "Sir, do not travel at night—these too are to be feared."
translations.idiomatic: In all his years in the hills he never met poisonous snakes or wild beasts; someone warned him, "You should not travel at night—that too can be dangerous."

sentences.zh: 文曰：「無心則無所畏。」

translations.literal: Wen said: "Without mind there is nothing to fear."
translations.idiomatic: Kong Wen replied, "Without selfish intent there is nothing to fear."

sentences.zh: 晚年惟玩《周易》、《老子》，他書亦不復讀。

translations.literal: In his later years he only delighted in the Zhou Changes and Laozi; other books he no longer read.
translations.idiomatic: In old age he read only the Book of Changes and the Laozi, and put all other books aside.

sentences.zh: 為《太玄圖》張壁上，外列方州部家，而規其中心，空之無所書。

translations.literal: He made a Diagram of the Supreme Mystery and spread it on the wall, on the outside arraying region, prefecture, department, and family, while ruling its center and leaving it empty with nothing written.
translations.idiomatic: He hung on his wall a chart of the Supreme Mystery with the outer rings of region, prefecture, department, and family marked out, while the center circle was left blank.

sentences.zh: 曰：「《易》所謂寂然不動者，與此無異也。」

translations.literal: He said: "What the Changes calls 'silent and unmoving' is no different from this."
translations.idiomatic: He said, "This is no different from what the Book of Changes calls 'still and unmoving.'"

sentences.zh: 何群，字通夫，果州西充人。

translations.literal: He Qun, styled Tongfu, was a man of Xichong in Guozhou.
translations.idiomatic: He Qun, whose courtesy name was Tongfu, came from Xichong in Guo Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 嗜古學，喜激揚論議，雖業進士，非其好也。

translations.literal: He was addicted to ancient learning, delighted in stirring and raising discourse; though he pursued the jinshi, it was not his preference.
translations.idiomatic: He loved classical learning and spirited debate; though he studied for the jinshi degree, examinations were not his true interest.

sentences.zh: 慶曆中，石介在太學，四方諸生來學者數千人，群亦自蜀至。

translations.literal: In the Qingli era Shi Jie was at the Imperial Academy; students coming to study from the four quarters numbered several thousand, and Qun also came from Shu.
translations.idiomatic: During the Qingli era Shi Jie taught at the Imperial University; thousands of students came from all over the empire, and He Qun traveled from Shu to join them.

sentences.zh: 方講官會諸生講，介曰：「生等知何群乎？

translations.literal: Just as the lecturer was meeting the students in lecture, Jie said: "Students, do you know He Qun?
translations.idiomatic: During a lecture to the assembled students, Shi Jie asked, "Do you know He Qun?

sentences.zh: 群日思為仁義而已，不知饑寒之切己也。」

translations.literal: Qun daily thinks only of practicing humaneness and righteousness, and does not know hunger and cold as pressing upon himself."
translations.idiomatic: He Qun thinks only of humaneness and righteousness from day to day, as though hunger and cold scarcely touched him."

sentences.zh: 眾皆注仰之。

translations.literal: The multitude all fixed their gaze upward on him.
translations.idiomatic: The students looked up to him with admiration.

sentences.zh: 介因館群於其家，使弟子推以為學長。

translations.literal: Jie thereupon lodged Qun in his home and had his disciples elevate him as chief of study.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Jie then took He Qun into his home and had his disciples treat him as their senior fellow student.

sentences.zh: 群愈自克厲，著書數十篇，與人言未嘗下意曲從，同舍目群為「白衣御史」。

translations.literal: Qun became ever more self-restrained and severe, authored several tens of chapters; in speaking with people he never lowered his intent or bent to follow, and his roommates called Qun "the Censor in plain clothes."
translations.idiomatic: He Qun disciplined himself still further, wrote dozens of essays, and in debate never lowered his principles to please others; his classmates nicknamed him "the censor in white robes."

sentences.zh: 群嘗言：「今之士，語言說易，舉止惰肆者，其衣冠不如古之嚴也。」

translations.literal: Qun once said: "Today's scholars, whose speech is facile in explanation and whose bearing is lazy and unrestrained—their caps and robes are not as strict as those of antiquity."
translations.idiomatic: He Qun once remarked, "Today's scholars speak glibly and conduct themselves loosely—their dress is far less dignified than that of the ancients."

sentences.zh: 因請復古衣冠。

translations.literal: He thereupon requested restoration of ancient caps and robes.
translations.idiomatic: He therefore petitioned to restore the ancient style of dress.

sentences.zh: 又上書言：「三代取士，皆舉於鄉里而先行義。

translations.literal: He also submitted a memorial saying: "The Three Dynasties selected scholars all by recommendation in the villages while first practicing righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: He also submitted a memorial stating, "In the Three Dynasties, scholars were chosen from their home districts only after they had first proven their moral conduct.

sentences.zh: 後世專以文辭就，文辭中害道者莫甚於賦，請罷去。」

translations.literal: Later ages rely solely on literary composition for selection; among literary forms nothing harms the Way more than fu-rhapsody—I request that it be abolished."
translations.idiomatic: Later ages select scholars solely through literary composition, and among literary forms nothing does more harm to the Way than the fu-rhapsody. I ask that it be abolished."

sentences.zh: 介讚美其說。

translations.literal: Jie praised his doctrine.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Jie praised his proposal.

sentences.zh: 會諫官御史亦言以賦取士無益治道，下兩製議，皆以為進士科始隋曆唐數百年，將相多出此，不為不得人，且祖宗行之已久，不可廢也。

translations.literal: At the time remonstrance officials and censors also said that selecting scholars by fu was of no benefit to the way of governance; the matter was sent down to the two academies for discussion, and all held that the jinshi examination began in Sui and passed through Tang for several hundred years, that generals and chief ministers mostly came from it—it was not that worthy men were not obtained—and moreover the ancestors had practiced it long; it could not be abolished.
translations.idiomatic: At the same time remonstrance officials and censors argued that selecting scholars through fu-rhapsodies did nothing for good government. The matter was referred to the Hanlin and academies for discussion. All agreed that the jinshi examination had begun in the Sui and continued through the Tang for centuries, that most generals and chief ministers had come from it, that worthy men were indeed found thereby, and that the ancestors had practiced it for so long that it could not be abolished.

sentences.zh: 群聞其說不行，乃慟哭，取平生所為賦八百餘篇焚之。

translations.literal: Qun heard that his doctrine would not be carried out; he then wept bitterly, took the more than eight hundred fu he had composed in his life, and burned them.
translations.idiomatic: When Qun learned that his proposal would not be adopted, he wept bitterly, gathered the more than eight hundred fu he had written in his lifetime, and burned them all.

sentences.zh: 講官視群賦既多且工，以為不情，絀出太學。

translations.literal: The lecturers, seeing that Qun's fu were both numerous and accomplished, thought this insincere and expelled him from the Imperial Academy.
translations.idiomatic: The lecturers, seeing that Qun's fu were both numerous and accomplished, judged his burning of them insincere and expelled him from the Imperial Academy.

sentences.zh: 群徑歸，遂不復舉進士。

translations.literal: Qun went straight home and thereafter never again took the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: Qun went straight home and never again sat for the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 嘉祐中，龍圖閣直學士何剡表其行義，賜號安逸處士。

translations.literal: In the Jiayou era, Hanlin academician He Yan memorialized his conduct and righteousness, and he was granted the title Recluse of Ease and Comfort.
translations.idiomatic: During the Jiayou era, academician He Yan memorialized his conduct and righteousness, and the court granted him the title Recluse of Ease and Comfort.

sentences.zh: 群既死，趙抃守益州，奏群遺稿有益時政，願詔果州錄上之，云：「非若茂陵書起天子侈心也。」

translations.literal: After Qun died, Zhao Bian guarded Yizhou and memorialized that Qun's posthumous writings were beneficial to current government, wishing that an edict order Guo Prefecture to record and submit them, saying, "They are not like the Maoling writings that aroused the Son of Heaven's extravagant heart."
translations.idiomatic: After Qun died, Zhao Bian, governor of Yizhou, memorialized that Qun's posthumous writings would benefit current government and asked that an edict order Guo Prefecture to copy and submit them, adding, "They are not like the writings of Maoling that stirred the emperor's taste for extravagance."

sentences.zh: 寢不下。

translations.literal: The matter was shelved and no edict issued.
translations.idiomatic: The proposal was shelved and no edict was issued.
